sentences.zh: 武大烈，臨潼人。

translations.literal: Wu Dalie was a native of Lintong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dalie was a native of Lintong.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟七年鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the seventh year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，授永寧知縣。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he was appointed magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era he was appointed magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 奸人倚萬安郡王恣不法，大烈痛懲之。

translations.literal: Wicked men relied on the Prince of the Wan'an commandery to behave lawlessly with impunity; Dalie punished them severely.
translations.idiomatic: Local ruffians took cover under the Prince of Wan'an and ran riot; Dalie punished them without mercy.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，李自成自南陽陷宜陽，知縣唐啟泰被害，遂攻永寧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year, Li Zicheng from Nanyang took Yiyang; Magistrate Tang Qitai was killed, and he then attacked Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year thirteen, Li Zicheng marched from Nanyang, seized Yiyang, and killed Magistrate Tang Qitai before turning on Yongning.

sentences.zh: 大烈與鄉官四川巡撫張論協力捍禦。

translations.literal: Dalie, together with a local elder and Zhang Lun, Governor-General of Sichuan, made a concerted defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dalie joined forces with a local elder and Zhang Lun, governor-general of Sichuan, to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 論歿，子吏部郎中鼎延及從父治中讃繼之。

translations.literal: When Lun died, his son Dingyan, a Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and his father's younger cousin Zan, the Administrative Assistant, took over.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun died, his son Dingyan—then a director in the Ministry of Personnel—and his father's younger cousin Zan, an administrative assistant, carried on the defense.

sentences.zh: 有獄囚勾賊入，都司馬有義棄城走。

translations.literal: A prisoner in custody colluded with the bandits to let them in; Vice Commander-in-Chief Ma Youyi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A jail inmate guided the rebels inside; Vice Commander Ma Youyi abandoned the walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 大烈、鼎延等固守三日，賊夜半登城，執大烈。

translations.literal: Dalie, Dingyan, and the others held firm for three days; at midnight the bandits scaled the wall and seized Dalie.
translations.idiomatic: Dalie and Dingyan held out for three days until, at midnight, the rebels climbed the wall and captured Dalie.

sentences.zh: 自成以同鄉欲活之，大烈不屈，索印又不予，乃燔灼以死。

translations.literal: Zicheng, as a fellow townsman, wished to spare his life, but Dalie would not submit; when asked for the seal he refused to hand it over, and they burned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng, recognizing a fellow townsman, offered to spare him; Dalie would not yield, and when they demanded the official seal he refused—so they burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 鼎延匿眢井免。

translations.literal: Dingyan hid in a blind well and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyan concealed himself in a disused well and survived.

sentences.zh: 讃及子國學生祚延死之。

translations.literal: Zan and his son Zuoyan, a student at the Imperial Academy, died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and his son Zuoyan, a student at the Imperial Academy, were killed.

sentences.zh: 主簿魏國輔、教諭任維清、守備王正己、百戶孫世英並不屈死。

translations.literal: Registrar Wei Guofu, Instructor Ren Weiqing, Garrison Commander Wang Zhengji, and Centennial Sun Shiying all refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Wei Guofu, Instructor Ren Weiqing, Garrison Commander Wang Zhengji, and company commander Sun Shiying all refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 萬安王采钅輕亦被害。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wan'an, Cai Qing, was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wan'an, Cai Qing, was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 賊移攻偃師，一日而陷。

translations.literal: The bandits shifted their attack to Yanshi, which fell in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moved on to Yanshi, which fell within a day.

sentences.zh: 知縣徐日泰大罵不屈，為賊臠割死。

translations.literal: Magistrate Xu Ritai cursed them loudly and would not yield; the bandits dismembered him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xu Ritai reviled them and would not submit; the rebels cut him apart while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 啟泰，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Qitai was a native of Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai was from Yexian.

sentences.zh: 日泰，金谿人。

translations.literal: Ritai was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ritai was from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 並起家鄉舉。

translations.literal: Both had begun their careers as provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Both had entered office through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊陷寶豐，知縣朱由椷死之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, the bandits took Baofeng; Magistrate Zhu Youqin died in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the rebels seized Baofeng; Magistrate Zhu Youqin died defending it.

sentences.zh: 陷密縣，知縣朱敏汀及裏居太仆卿魏持衡、舉人馬體健死之。

translations.literal: They took Mi County; Magistrate Zhu Minting, along with Wei Chiheng, retired Grand Master of the Stud, and graduate Ma Tijian, who lived locally, all died.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Mi County; Magistrate Zhu Minting, the retired Grand Master of the Stud Wei Chiheng, and the local graduate Ma Tijian all perished.

sentences.zh: 由椷，益府鎮國將軍常澈子，敏汀亦宗室，並由貢生。

translations.literal: Youqin was son of Chang Che, State Defender General of the Yi Princely Establishment; Minting was also of imperial lineage; both had entered office through the tribute-student route.
translations.idiomatic: Youqin was the son of Chang Che, Defender General of the Yi princely establishment; Minting was also of the imperial clan; both had risen through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 敏汀妾張，一女一孫及臧獲數人俱死，與由椷並贈僉事。

translations.literal: Minting's concubine Zhang, a daughter, a grandson, and several servants all died; he and Youqin were both posthumously granted the rank of Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Minting's concubine Zhang, a daughter, a grandson, and several household servants died with them; both men were posthumously granted the rank of vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是月，陷洛陽，鄉官來秉衡、劉芳奕、常克念、郭顯星、韓金聲、王明、楊萃、荀良翰等抗節死。

translations.literal: That month they took Luoyang; local elders Lai Bingheng, Liu Fangyi, Chang Kenian, Guo Xianxing, Han Jinsheng, Wang Ming, Yang Cui, and Xun Lianghan and others died resisting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Luoyang fell; the local elders Lai Bingheng, Liu Fangyi, Chang Kenian, Guo Xianxing, Han Jinsheng, Wang Ming, Yang Cui, Xun Lianghan, and others died holding to their integrity.

sentences.zh: 秉衡，天啟四年舉於鄉，未仕。

translations.literal: Bingheng passed the provincial examination in the fourth year of Tianqi but had not yet taken office.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng had passed the provincial examination in Tianqi year four but had not yet taken office.

sentences.zh: 城陷，為賊將劉宗敏所執，令易服，欲官之，不可。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized by the bandit general Liu Zongmin, who ordered him to change clothes and wished to give him office; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken by the rebel general Liu Zongmin, who ordered him to change his dress and offered him a post; he refused.

sentences.zh: 羈南郊民舍，顧見其友，謂之曰：「賊勒我以官，我義不受辱，恨母老子幼，死不瞑目爾。」

translations.literal: Held in a civilian house in the southern suburbs, he saw a friend and said to him: "The bandits are pressing me to accept office; by duty I cannot endure disgrace, but I grieve that my mother is old and my son young—I cannot close my eyes in death.
translations.idiomatic: Confined in a farmhouse in the southern suburbs, he caught sight of a friend and said, "The rebels are forcing an office on me; by right I cannot bear such shame—yet my mother is old and my son still young, and I cannot die with my eyes at rest.

sentences.zh: 賊聞，燒鐵索加其脛，終不從，遂被殺，並其母劉、妾吳及幼子俱殺之。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard this, they heated iron chains and applied them to his shins; he still would not yield and was killed, together with his mother Liu, concubine Wu, and young son.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard this, they heated iron fetters and clamped them to his legs; he still would not submit, and they killed him—together with his mother Liu, concubine Wu, and young son.

sentences.zh: 芳奕，慷慨負智略，與秉衡同舉於鄉，為昌樂知縣。

translations.literal: Fangyi was generous in spirit and possessed resourcefulness; he had passed the provincial examination the same year as Bingheng and served as magistrate of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi was open-handed and shrewd; he had passed the provincial examination together with Bingheng and served as magistrate of Changle.

sentences.zh: 解官歸，歲大歉，人相食，傾橐濟之。

translations.literal: He resigned and returned home; in a year of great famine people ate one another, and he emptied his coffers to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He left office and returned home; in a year of terrible famine people turned to cannibalism, and he spent his entire fortune on relief.

sentences.zh: 賊漸逼，集義士為幹城社，佐有司保障。

translations.literal: As the bandits drew near, he gathered men of honor into a Gancheng Society to assist the officials in defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels closed in, he rallied worthy men into a Gancheng Society to help the officials defend the city.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，縊死西城戍樓。

translations.literal: When the city fell he hanged himself on the watchtower at the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he hanged himself in the watchtower at the western gate.

sentences.zh: 克念舉進士，為平陽推官，有聲。

translations.literal: Kenian had passed the metropolitan examination and served as investigating censor in Pingyang, with a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Kenian was a metropolitan graduate who served as investigating censor in Pingyang and enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 顯星舉於鄉，為翰林待詔。

translations.literal: Xianxing had passed the provincial examination and was a Hanlin awaiting-edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxing had passed the provincial examination and held a Hanlin awaiting-edict post.

sentences.zh: 金聲、明，皆進士。

translations.literal: Jinsheng and Ming were both metropolitan graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng and Ming were both metropolitan graduates.

sentences.zh: 金聲官邯鄲知縣，明官行人。

translations.literal: Jinsheng served as magistrate of Handan; Ming served as courier of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng had been magistrate of Handan; Ming had served as a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 萃、良翰皆舉人。

translations.literal: Cui and Lianghan were both provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Cui and Lianghan were both provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 萃官辰州知府，良翰未仕。

translations.literal: Cui held office as prefect of Chenzhou; Lianghan had not yet served.
translations.idiomatic: Cui was prefect of Chenzhou; Lianghan had not yet taken office.

sentences.zh: 錢祚徵，字錫吉，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Qian Zuozheng, courtesy name Xiji, was a native of Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zuozheng, style name Xiji, was a native of Yexian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，由鄉舉歷官汝州知州。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he rose through the provincial examination to become prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era he advanced through the provincial examination to prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 汝為流賊往來孔道，土寇又竊據山中。

translations.literal: Ruzhou lay on a main thoroughfare for roving bandits, and local bandits also held the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou stood on a main corridor for roving rebels, while local bandits also held the hills.

sentences.zh: 祚徵欲先除土寇，募壯士千人訓練，而遣人為好言招撫，夜半取間道直搗其巢，寇大敗。

translations.literal: Zuozheng wished first to eliminate the local bandits; he recruited a thousand stalwart men for training, sent envoys with conciliatory words to induce surrender, and at midnight took a secret path straight to their lair—the bandits were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuozheng resolved to clear out the hill bandits first: he recruited a thousand strong men for drill, sent men with soothing words to coax surrender, then at midnight took a hidden route straight to their nest and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 乃令民千家立一大寨，有急鳴鉦相救，寇勢衰息，其魁遂降。

translations.literal: He then ordered every thousand households to establish one large stockade; in emergency they would strike a gong to summon aid, the bandits' strength dwindled, and their chief eventually surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then required every thousand households to form one great stockade; at alarm they would ring a gong for mutual rescue, the bandits' power waned, and their leader finally submitted.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，李自成驟來犯，祚徵乘城守，身中流矢，守益力。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year Li Zicheng suddenly came to attack; Zuozheng defended from the walls, was struck by a stray arrow, and redoubled his efforts in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year fourteen Li Zicheng struck without warning; Zuozheng fought from the walls, took an arrow wound, and defended all the harder.

sentences.zh: 月余，大風霾，炮炸樓焚，城遂陷，罵賊而死。

translations.literal: After more than a month, a great wind blew with dust haze; cannon fire exploded, the tower burned, the city fell, and he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month a fierce wind brought murk and dust; a cannon burst, the tower caught fire, the city fell, and he reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 汝人立廟祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Ru erected a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ru built a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 盛以恒，潼關衛人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yiheng was a native of Tongguan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yiheng was a native of Tongguan Guard.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十三年舉人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year thirteen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 知商城縣。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Shangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shangcheng.

sentences.zh: 視事月余，流賊突至，卻之。

translations.literal: Within a month of taking office the roving bandits suddenly arrived; he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month into his term the roving rebels appeared; he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 明年，張獻忠陷襄陽，鄰境大恐。

translations.literal: The following year Zhang Xianzhong took Xiangyang, and neighboring districts were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Xianzhong seized Xiangyang, and the neighboring prefectures were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 以恒已遷開封同知，將行，士民懇留之，乃登陴，與鄉官楊所修、洪胤衡、馬剛中、段增輝共城守。

translations.literal: Yiheng had already been transferred to Vice Prefect of Kaifeng and was about to depart; the gentry and commoners earnestly begged him to stay; he mounted the ramparts and, with local elders Yang Suoxiu, Hong Yinheng, Ma Gangzhong, and Duan Zenghui, jointly defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng had already been promoted to vice prefect of Kaifeng and was preparing to leave, but gentry and commoners pleaded with him to remain; he climbed the battlements and, with local elders Yang Suoxiu, Hong Yinheng, Ma Gangzhong, and Duan Zenghui, held the city together.

sentences.zh: 二月中，賊奄至，適雨雪，守者凍餒不能戰。

translations.literal: In the second month the bandits suddenly arrived; it happened to rain and snow, and the defenders, frozen and starving, could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the rebels appeared without warning; rain and snow fell, and the defenders, numb with cold and hunger, could not hold the line.

sentences.zh: 以恒督家眾射賊十七人墜馬，賊怒，並力攻，矢中以恒右額，猶裹創拒敵。

translations.literal: Yiheng led his household retainers in shooting down seventeen bandits from their horses; the bandits in anger attacked with combined force; an arrow struck Yiheng on the right forehead, yet he still bound his wound and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng directed his household archers and brought seventeen rebels down from their horses; enraged, the enemy pressed the assault; an arrow struck him on the right brow, yet he bound the wound and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊登北城，家眾巷戰死且盡，乃被執，罵賊不屈，為賊支解。

translations.literal: The bandits scaled the north wall; the household fought in the lanes until nearly all were dead; he was then seized, cursed the bandits and would not yield, and was dismembered by them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took the north wall; his household died fighting in the alleys until almost none remained; he was captured, reviled them and refused to submit, and they cut him apart.

sentences.zh: 孫覺及典史呂維顯、教諭曹維正皆死。

translations.literal: Sun Jue, along with Registrar Lü Weixian and Instructor Cao Weizheng, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jue, Registrar Lü Weixian, and Instructor Cao Weizheng all perished.

sentences.zh: 所修，故魏忠賢黨也。

translations.literal: Suoxiu had formerly been a member of Wei Zhongxian's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Suoxiu had once belonged to Wei Zhongxian's faction.

sentences.zh: 歷左副都御史，入逆案，贖徒為民，至是罵賊死。

translations.literal: He had served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, was implicated in the case of the partisans, ransomed himself to commoner status, and on this occasion cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, was caught in the partisan case, bought his way back to commoner status, and now reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 胤衡，萬歷中進士。

translations.literal: Yinheng was a metropolitan graduate in the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yinheng passed the metropolitan examination in the Wanli era.

sentences.zh: 歷官陽和兵備副使，分守北門，力戰死。

translations.literal: He had served as Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Yanghe, held the north gate in divided defense, and died fighting hard.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as Yanghe military vice commissioner, held the northern gate in the defense, and died in fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 剛中，字九如。

translations.literal: Gangzhong, courtesy name Jiuru.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong, style name Jiuru.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year seven.

sentences.zh: 除大同知縣，行取授檢討，乞假歸。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Datong, selected for promotion and made a reviser, then begged leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Datong, selected for the Hanlin as reviser, then took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 賊入，大罵，被磔死。

translations.literal: When the bandits entered he cursed them loudly and was dismembered alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered he reviled them and was torn apart alive.

sentences.zh: 增輝，字含素，為諸生，以學行稱。

translations.literal: Zenghui, courtesy name Hansu, was a student and was renowned for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zenghui, style name Hansu, was a licentiate famed for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 朝廷下保舉令，被薦，不樂為吏，擬除教授，未謁選歸。

translations.literal: When the court issued a recommendation order he was nominated but was unwilling to serve as an official; he was slated for appointment as professor but returned home before presenting himself for selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the court called for recommendations he was named but disliked official service; he was slated for a professorship but went home before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 遇變，罵賊死。

translations.literal: When the crisis came he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck he reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 賊既陷商城，即疾驅犯信陽。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had taken Shangcheng they swiftly marched to attack Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Shangcheng fell the rebels raced against Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 城陷，知州高孝志，訓導李逢旭、程所聞，裏居靜海知縣張映宿死之。

translations.literal: The city fell; Prefect Gao Xiaozhi, Instructors Li Fengxu and Cheng Suowen, and Zhang Yingsu, retired magistrate of Jinghai, who lived locally, all died.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Prefect Gao Xiaozhi, Instructors Li Fengxu and Cheng Suowen, and Zhang Yingsu, the retired Jinghai magistrate living at home, all died.

sentences.zh: 其陷光山，典史魏光遠亦死之。

translations.literal: When they took Guangshan, Registrar Wei Guangyuan also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangshan fell, Registrar Wei Guangyuan died as well.

sentences.zh: 所司請贈恤，未報。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested posthumous honors, but no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices petitioned for posthumous rewards, but no response came.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月，帝下詔曰：「比州縣有司不設守備，賊至即陷，與沖鋒陷陣，持久力詘者殊科。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year the Emperor issued an edict saying: "Of late the prefectural and county officials have made no defensive preparations; when bandits arrive the places fall at once—this is a wholly different matter from those who charge the battle line, hold out long, and exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year fifteen the Emperor decreed: "Lately prefectural and county officials have kept no defenses ready; when rebels come the place falls at once—this is not the same as men who charge the line, hold out to the end, and spend their strength to the last.

sentences.zh: 若概援天啟間例，優予贈蔭，何由旌勸勞臣。

translations.literal: If one uniformly applied the Tianqi-era precedents and granted generous posthumous titles and hereditary privileges, how could meritorious ministers be encouraged and rewarded?
translations.idiomatic: If we applied the Tianqi precedents across the board and lavished posthumous titles and hereditary privileges, how would we distinguish and reward those who truly earned it?

sentences.zh: 自今五品以下，止贈監司，四品及方面，始贈京卿。

translations.literal: From now on, officials of the fifth rank and below shall receive posthumous titles only up to surveillance commissioner; the fourth rank and regional posts may receive capital ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth fifth-rank officials and below receive posthumous titles only to surveillance commissioner; fourth-rank and regional posts may receive capital ministers.

sentences.zh: 著為令。」

translations.literal: This was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This was made a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 乃贈以恒副使，孝志參議，維顯等贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Yiheng was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner; Xiaozhi, Assistant Commissioner; Weixian and others received differentiated posthumous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng was posthumously made vice commissioner; Xiaozhi, assistant commissioner; Weixian and the rest received graded posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，州縣長吏殉難者，率贈京卿，蔭錦衣世職，賜祭葬，有司建祠。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi era, when prefectural and county chiefs died for the state, they were generally granted posthumous titles as capital ministers, hereditary privileges in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, sacrificial rites and burial honors, and temples built by the local offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, prefectural and county chiefs who died in office were usually posthumously made capital ministers, granted hereditary Embroidered-Uniform Guard posts, sacrificial rites and state burial, and local temples.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，改蔭國子生，俾之出仕，而京卿之贈如故，至是始改贈外僚雲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen the hereditary privilege was changed to enrollment in the Imperial Academy with permission to enter office, while the capital-minister posthumous title remained as before; only now was the posthumous grant to outside officials changed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen the hereditary privilege was changed to Imperial Academy enrollment with permission to serve, while capital-minister posthumous titles stayed the same; only now were outside officials given the revised grants.

sentences.zh: 顏日愉，字華陽，上虞人。

translations.literal: Yan Riyu, courtesy name Huayang, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Riyu, style name Huayang, was from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the Wanli era.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，除知葉縣，有惠政，為上官所惡，劾罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Ye County; he had benevolent policies but was hated by his superiors and was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he became magistrate of Ye County; his humane rule won the people but his superiors hated him and had him impeached out of office.

sentences.zh: 部民爭詣闕訟冤，乃獲敘用。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture went in a body to the capital to plead his innocence, and he was then allowed to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: The people marched to court to protest his innocence, and he was restored to service.

sentences.zh: 後為靜寧知州。

translations.literal: Later he served as prefect of Jingning.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Jingning.

sentences.zh: 羅賊亂，馳請固鎮五道兵合剿。

translations.literal: When Luo bandits rose in disorder he urgently requested the five-route troops of Guzhen to join in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo bandits rebelled he urgently called for the five-route troops of Guzhen to join a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 而先率敢死士數人招諭之，賊弛備，遂遣精卒搗其營，賊倉皇潰，斬數百級。

translations.literal: But first he led several dare-to-die men to summon and instruct them; the bandits relaxed their guard; he then sent picked troops to strike their camp; the bandits fled in panic and several hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: First he led a few dare-to-die men to summon and admonish them; the rebels let down their guard; he then sent elite troops to storm their camp; they broke in panic and several hundred were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 黎明，五道兵繼至，復大破之。

translations.literal: At dawn the five-route troops arrived and inflicted another great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the five-route army came up and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 遷開封同知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 流賊勢方熾，上官以南陽要沖，舉日愉為知府，大治守具，人心稍固。

translations.literal: Roving bandits were then at their height; his superiors, because Nanyang was a strategic crossroads, recommended Riyu as prefect; he greatly improved the defenses, and morale steadied somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: With roving rebels raging, his superiors, seeing Nanyang as a vital crossroads, recommended Riyu as prefect; he greatly strengthened the defenses and hearts steadied a little.

sentences.zh: 十四年五月，賊猝至，百余人冒雨登城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year the bandits suddenly arrived; more than a hundred men climbed the wall in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year fourteen the rebels struck without warning; over a hundred men scaled the wall in the rain.

sentences.zh: 日愉擊殺之幾盡，余賊引去，城獲全。

translations.literal: Riyu struck and killed nearly all of them; the remaining bandits withdrew and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Riyu struck and killed nearly all of them; the survivors withdrew and the city held.

sentences.zh: 日愉手中一矢，頭項被二刃，死城上。

translations.literal: Riyu had one arrow in his hand; his head and neck received two blades, and he died on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Riyu took one arrow in the hand; two blades struck head and neck, and he died on the wall.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太僕卿。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted the title of Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 賊既不得誌去，遂縱掠旁近州縣。

translations.literal: The bandits, unable to achieve their aim, withdrew and then ravaged the neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated of their aim, the rebels withdrew and plundered the neighboring prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 其冬再圍南陽，攻陷之，參議艾毓初死焉。

translations.literal: That winter they besieged Nanyang again, took it, and Assistant Commissioner Ai Yuchu died there.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they besieged Nanyang again, captured it, and Assistant Commissioner Ai Yuchu died there.

sentences.zh: 毓初，字孩如，米脂人，戶部侍郎希淳曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yuchu, courtesy name Hairu, was a native of Mizhi and great-grandson of Vice Minister of Revenue Ai Xichun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchu, style name Hairu, was from Mizhi and great-grandson of Vice Minister of Revenue Ai Xichun.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year four.

sentences.zh: 授內鄉知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Neixiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Neixiang.

sentences.zh: 生長邊陲，習戰事。

translations.literal: Raised on the frontier, he was versed in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the borderlands, he knew warfare.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，流寇來犯。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year roving bandits came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year six roving rebels attacked.

sentences.zh: 埋大炮名「滾地龍」者於城外，城中燃線發之，賊死無算，遂解去。

translations.literal: He buried outside the walls great guns called "Rolling Earth Dragons"; lines were fired from within the city to detonate them, and the bandits died beyond counting and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He buried outside the walls great guns called "Rolling Earth Dragons"; fuses were lit from within the city, the rebels died beyond counting, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 內鄉與領邑淅川多深山邃谷，為盜窟，民居懍懍。

translations.literal: Neixiang and the neighboring county Xichuan had many deep mountains and secluded valleys that served as bandit lairs; the people lived in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Neixiang and neighboring Xichuan had deep mountains and hidden valleys that sheltered bandits; the people lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 毓初至，為設守備，民得少安。

translations.literal: When Yuchu arrived he established defensive posts and the people gained a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchu arrived he set up defenses and the people breathed a little easier.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，唐王聿鍵上言：「祖制，親王所封地，有司早晚必謁見。

translations.literal: The next winter Prince Tang Zhu Yujian memorialized: "By ancestral regulation, in the territory granted to imperial princes the local officials must pay their respects morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Prince Tang Zhu Yujian memorialized: "By ancestral rule, in a prince's grant the local officials must attend morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 今艾毓初等皆不謁。」

translations.literal: Now Ai Yuchu and the others have not paid their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ai Yuchu and the others have not attended.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，悉逮下法司，而敕禮部申典制。

translations.literal: The Emperor in anger had them all arrested and sent to the judiciary, while ordering the Ministry of Rites to clarify the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor in anger had them all arrested and sent to the judiciary, and ordered the Ministry of Rites to restate the regulations.

sentences.zh: 已而王被逮，毓初獲補官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the prince was arrested; Yuchu was able to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the prince himself was arrested; Yuchu was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 屢遷至右參議，分守南陽，與日愉卻賊有功。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner, holding divided defense at Nanyang, and with Riyu repelled the bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Assistant Commissioner, held divided defense at Nanyang, and with Riyu drove back the rebels with merit.

sentences.zh: 自成用宋獻策計，欲取南陽以圖關中，復率大眾來寇。

translations.literal: Zicheng, using Song Xiance's plan, wished to take Nanyang in order to advance on Guanzhong and again led a great host to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng, following Song Xiance's plan to take Nanyang and march on Guanzhong, again led a great army against the city.

sentences.zh: 毓初偕總兵官猛如虎等堅守。

translations.literal: Yuchu together with the regional commander Meng Ruhu and others held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchu joined Regional Commander Meng Ruhu and others in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 賊攻入南門，會總督楊文嶽援軍至，賊引退。

translations.literal: The bandits broke in through the south gate; just then the relief army of Governor-General Yang Wenyue arrived and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke through the south gate; then Governor-General Yang Wenyue's relief army arrived and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文嶽去，賊復攻之，食盡援絕，毓初題詩城樓，遂自縊。

translations.literal: When Wenyue left the bandits attacked again; food and reinforcements were exhausted; Yuchu inscribed a poem on the city tower and then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyue departed the rebels attacked again; provisions and relief ran out; Yuchu wrote a poem on the tower and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 南陽知縣姚運熙、主簿門迎恩、訓導楊氣開亦死之。

translations.literal: Nanyang Magistrate Yao Yunxi, Registrar Men Ying'en, and Instructor Yang Qikai also died.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang Magistrate Yao Yunxi, Registrar Men Ying'en, and Instructor Yang Qikai died as well.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，自成再陷南陽，知府丘懋素罵賊不屈，闔門被害。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year Zicheng again took Nanyang; Prefect Qiu Maosu cursed the bandits and would not yield, and his whole household was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year Zicheng again took Nanyang; Prefect Qiu Maosu reviled the rebels and would not submit, and his entire household was killed.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊過扶溝，眾議城守，舉人劉恩澤初嘗以策幹當事，多見用。

translations.literal: That month, as the bandits passed Fugou, the people debated defending the city; the graduate Liu Enze had once offered stratagems to the authorities and was much relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: That month, as the rebels passed Fugou, the town debated defense; Graduate Liu Enze had once offered plans to the authorities and was much heeded.

sentences.zh: 縣令騃不解事，恩澤痛哭曰：「吾不幸從木偶人死。」

translations.literal: The magistrate was dull and understood nothing; Enze wept and said: "Alas that I must die with a wooden puppet.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was obtuse and useless; Enze wept and said, "Wretched that I must die with a wooden puppet.

sentences.zh: 自題樓壁曰：「千古綱常事，男兒肯讓人。」

translations.literal: He inscribed on the tower wall: "The eternal bonds of right and wrong—will a man yield them to another?"
translations.idiomatic: On the tower wall he wrote: "The eternal bonds of right and wrong—would a true man yield them to another?"

sentences.zh: 明日，城陷，擲樓下以死。

translations.literal: The next day the city fell; he threw himself from the tower and died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell; he cast himself from the tower and died.

sentences.zh: 潘弘，字若稚，淮安山陽人。

translations.literal: Pan Hong, courtesy name Ruozhi, was a native of Shanyang in Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hong, style name Ruozhi, was from Shanyang in Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 起家貢生。

translations.literal: He began his career as a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十三年為舞陽知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he became magistrate of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year thirteen he became magistrate of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 時流賊披猖，土寇亦間發，弘數討敗之。

translations.literal: At that time roving bandits ran wild and local bandits also rose intermittently; Hong repeatedly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Roving rebels were rampant and local bandits also flared up; Hong repeatedly routed them.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，李自成、羅汝才既陷南陽，縱兵覆所屬州縣，將攻舞陽，弘諭士民共拒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the following year Li Zicheng and Luo Rucai, having already taken Nanyang, spread their troops over the subordinate prefectures and counties and were about to attack Wuyang; Hong urged gentry and commoners to resist together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the next year Li Zicheng and Luo Rucai, having taken Nanyang, overran the subordinate prefectures and counties and were about to strike Wuyang; Hong urged gentry and people to resist together.

sentences.zh: 諸生慮賊屠城，請委曲紓禍，弘叱之去。

translations.literal: The students, fearing the bandits would massacre the city, asked to placate the disaster by compromise; Hong rebuked them and drove them away.
translations.idiomatic: The students, fearing massacre, begged to soften the blow by compromise; Hong rebuked them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 賊薄城，發炮擊之，多斃。

translations.literal: When the bandits pressed the city he fired cannon and struck them; many were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels pressed the walls he fired cannon and killed many.

sentences.zh: 有小校善射，屢卻賊。

translations.literal: There was a junior officer skilled in archery who repeatedly drove the bandits back.
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer skilled with the bow repeatedly drove them back.

sentences.zh: 諸生潛遣人約降，賊復至。

translations.literal: The students secretly sent men to arrange surrender; the bandits came again.
translations.idiomatic: The students secretly sent men to arrange surrender; the rebels returned.

sentences.zh: 弘作告先聖文，自誓必死。

translations.literal: Hong composed a memorial to the Sage and swore he would certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: Hong wrote a memorial to the Sage and vowed he would die.

sentences.zh: 諸生潛開門，縛弘以獻。

translations.literal: The students secretly opened the gate and bound Hong to present him.
translations.idiomatic: The students secretly opened the gate and bound Hong to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 賊索印，弘不予。

translations.literal: The bandits demanded the seal; Hong would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels demanded the seal; Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 脅降，怒罵不屈，乃支解之。

translations.literal: They tried to force him to submit; he cursed them in anger and would not yield, and they dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to force his submission; he reviled them and would not yield, and they cut him apart.

sentences.zh: 子澄瀾痛憤大哭，投井死。

translations.literal: His son Cheng Lan wept in bitter grief and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng Lan wept in anguish and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 時鄧州、鎮平、內鄉、沁陽、新野相繼陷。

translations.literal: At that time Dengzhou, Zhenping, Neixiang, Qinyang, and Xinye fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then Dengzhou, Zhenping, Neixiang, Qinyang, and Xinye fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 鄧州知州劉振世，吏目李國璽，千戶余承蔭、李錫，諸生丁一統、張五美、王鐘、王子章、海寬、傅彥皆抗節死。

translations.literal: Dengzhou Prefect Liu Zhenshi, Clerk Li Guoxi, centurions Yu Chengyin and Li Xi, and students Ding Yitong, Zhang Wumei, Wang Zhong, Wang Zizhang, Hai Kuan, and Fu Yan all died holding to their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou Prefect Liu Zhenshi, Clerk Li Guoxi, centurions Yu Chengyin and Li Xi, and students Ding Yitong, Zhang Wumei, Wang Zhong, Wang Zizhang, Hai Kuan, and Fu Yan all died holding their integrity.

sentences.zh: 鎮平知縣成縣鐘其碩被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: Zhenping Magistrate Zhong Qishuo of Chengxian was seized, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenping Magistrate Zhong Qishuo of Chengxian was captured, reviled the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 內鄉知縣南昌龔新、新野知縣四川韓醇，並不屈死。

translations.literal: Neixiang Magistrate Gong Xin of Nanchang and Xinye Magistrate Han Chun of Sichuan both refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Neixiang Magistrate Gong Xin of Nanchang and Xinye Magistrate Han Chun of Sichuan both refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 泌陽凡再陷。

translations.literal: Biyang fell twice in all.
translations.idiomatic: Biyang fell twice in all.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，張獻忠破信陽，獲左良玉旗幟，假之以登城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year Zhang Xianzhong took Xinyang, seized Zuo Liangyu's banners, and used them falsely to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year Zhang Xianzhong took Xinyang, seized Zuo Liangyu's banners, and used them to trick their way onto the wall.

sentences.zh: 知縣雲南南寧王士昌懷印端坐，被縛，謾罵死。

translations.literal: Magistrate Wang Shichang of Nanning, Yunnan, sat upright holding the seal, was bound, reviled them, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wang Shichang of Nanning, Yunnan, sat upright with the seal in hand, was bound, reviled them, and died.

sentences.zh: 臨昌姚昌祚代之，甫數月，復陷。

translations.literal: Yao Changzuo of Linchang replaced him; within a few months it fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Changzuo of Linchang replaced him; within a few months the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 昌祚手斬數賊，力屈死。

translations.literal: Changzuo personally cut down several bandits and died when his strength gave out.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo personally cut down several rebels and died when his strength failed.

sentences.zh: 典史雷晉暹率捕卒戰死。

translations.literal: Registrar Lei Jinxian led constables in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Lei Jinxian led constables into battle and died.

sentences.zh: 又有武職王衍範、錢繼功、海成俱死難。

translations.literal: There were also military officers Wang Yanfan, Qian Jigong, and Hai Cheng who all died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers Wang Yanfan, Qian Jigong, and Hai Cheng also died in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 而鄧州於十年春為張獻忠所破，知州孫澤盛、同知薛應齡皆戰死，至是亦再陷雲。

translations.literal: Dengzhou had been broken by Zhang Xianzhong in the spring of the tenth year; Prefect Sun Zesheng and Vice Prefect Xue Yingling both died in battle; now it too fell a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou had been broken by Zhang Xianzhong in the spring of year ten; Prefect Sun Zesheng and Vice Prefect Xue Yingling had died fighting; now it fell again.

sentences.zh: 陳豫抱，舞陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Yubao was a native of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yubao was from Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 母段早寡，撫豫抱及其弟豫養、豫懷，皆為諸生，力田好學，善承母誌。

translations.literal: His mother Duan was widowed early; she raised Yubao and his younger brothers Yuyang and Yuhuai; all became students, tilled the fields and loved learning, and dutifully fulfilled their mother's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Duan was widowed young; she raised Yubao and his brothers Yuyang and Yuhuai; all became licentiates, farmed and loved learning, and faithfully carried out their mother's will.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年，流賊陷舞陽，母先赴井，三子從之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen the roving bandits took Wuyang; the mother first threw herself into a well and the three sons followed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year fourteen the roving rebels took Wuyang; the mother first entered a well and the three sons followed.

sentences.zh: 豫抱妻黃攜其子默通，豫養妻馬攜子默恒、默言俱從之。

translations.literal: Yubao's wife Huang took their son Motong; Yuyang's wife Ma took sons Moheng and Moyan—all followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yubao's wife Huang took their son Motong; Yuyang's wife Ma took sons Moheng and Moyan—all followed them.

sentences.zh: 三世九人，一時盡節。

translations.literal: Three generations, nine persons, all died for integrity at one time.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations, nine people, died for integrity at once.

sentences.zh: 時郡邑諸生死者甚眾，錄其著者。

translations.literal: At that time many graduates and officials in the prefectures and counties died; those of note are recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Many graduates and officials in the prefectures and counties died; the notable cases are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 內鄉許宣及二弟寀、宮，慷慨好義。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan of Neixiang and his two younger brothers Cai and Gong were generous and fond of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan of Neixiang and his younger brothers Cai and Gong were open-handed and devoted to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 賊陷鄧州，宣兄弟結里中壯士，直入其城，擒偽官，堅守許家寨。

translations.literal: When the bandits took Dengzhou, the Xuan brothers gathered stalwart men of the neighborhood, entered the city directly, seized the false officials, and held firm at the Xu family stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhou fell the Xu brothers rallied neighborhood stalwarts, entered the city, seized the puppet officials, and held the Xu family stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，攻破之，寀從母常先投井死，宣、宮皆詈賊被殺，宮妻鐘、寀妻陳並自經，其妹亦罵賊被殺。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger broke through it; Cai followed his mother Chang in throwing herself into a well first; Xuan and Gong both cursed the bandits and were killed; Gong's wife Zhong and Cai's wife Chen both hanged themselves; their sister also cursed the bandits and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in fury stormed it; Cai followed his mother Chang into a well first; Xuan and Gong reviled the rebels and were killed; Gong's wife Zhong and Cai's wife Chen hanged themselves; their sister too reviled the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 時稱「許氏七烈」。

translations.literal: At the time they were called "the seven martyrs of the Xu family."
translations.idiomatic: People called them "the seven martyrs of the Xu family."

sentences.zh: 賊之攻偃師也，張毓粹率二子佐有司固守，城陷，大罵，俱被殺。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked Yanshi, Zhang Cuicui led his two sons to assist the officials in a stubborn defense; when the city fell they cursed loudly and were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshi was attacked, Zhang Cuicui and his two sons helped the officials hold the walls; when the city fell they reviled the rebels and were all killed.

sentences.zh: 妻藺與三女、二孫悉赴井死。

translations.literal: His wife Lin and three daughters and two grandsons all threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lin, three daughters, and two grandsons all entered a well and died.

sentences.zh: 賊殺武同芳母，同芳噴血大罵，支解而死。

translations.literal: The bandits killed Wu Tongfang's mother; Tongfang spat blood and cursed them loudly and was dismembered and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels killed Wu Tongfang's mother; he spat blood, reviled them, and was cut apart.

sentences.zh: 劉芳名、劉芳世、藺之粹、喬於昆、藺完馪、王光顯、喬國屏、王邦紀、藺相裔、張一鷺、張一鵬、牛一元皆抗節死。

translations.literal: Liu Fangming, Liu Fangshi, Lan Zhicui, Qiao Yukun, Lan Wanxin, Wang Guangxian, Qiao Guoping, Wang Bangji, Lan Xiangyi, Zhang Yilu, Zhang Yipeng, and Niu Yiyuan all died holding to their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fangming, Liu Fangshi, Lan Zhicui, Qiao Yukun, Lan Wanxin, Wang Guangxian, Qiao Guoping, Wang Bangji, Lan Xiangyi, Zhang Yilu, Zhang Yipeng, and Niu Yiyuan all died holding their integrity.

sentences.zh: 芳名、完馪妻皆張氏，與邦紀妻高並從死。

translations.literal: Fangming's and Wanxin's wives were both surnamed Zhang; together with Bangji's wife Gao they followed their husbands in death.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming's and Wanxin's wives were both Zhangs; Gao, wife of Bangji, died with them as well.

sentences.zh: 一鷺、一鵬父亦罵賊死。

translations.literal: Yilu and Yipeng's father also cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: The father of Yilu and Yipeng also reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 唐縣許曰琮，早喪父。

translations.literal: Xu Yuecong of Tang County lost his father early.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuecong of Tang County was fatherless from youth.

sentences.zh: 母歿，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died he lived by her tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned at her tomb for three years.

sentences.zh: 城破，遁居南山。

translations.literal: When the city fell he fled to live on South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he hid on South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊徵之不出，脅以死，鐫其背曰：「誓不從賊」，遂嘔血而死。

translations.literal: The bandits summoned him but he would not come out; they threatened him with death and carved on his back the words "I swear never to follow the bandits"; he then vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels summoned him but he would not emerge; they threatened death and carved on his back, "I swear never to follow the rebels"; he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 劉振之，字而強，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhenzhi, courtesy name Erqiang, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenzhi, style name Erqiang, was from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 性剛方，敦學行，鄉人嚴重之。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and firm; he cultivated learning and conduct, and the people of his district held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and firm by nature, he devoted himself to learning and conduct, and his neighbors esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，舉於鄉，以教諭遷鄢陵知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination; from instructor he was transferred to magistrate of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination, rose from instructor to magistrate of Yanling.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月，李自成陷許州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year Li Zicheng took Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year fourteen Li Zicheng seized Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 知州王應翼被害，都司張守正，鄉官魏完真，諸生李文鵬、王應鵬皆死。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Yingyi was killed; Regional Commander Zhang Shouzheng, local elder Wei Wanzhen, and students Li Wenpeng and Wang Yingpeng all died.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Yingyi was killed; Regional Commander Zhang Shouzheng, local elder Wei Wanzhen, and students Li Wenpeng and Wang Yingpeng all perished.

sentences.zh: 自許以南無堅城。

translations.literal: South of Xu there was no strong city.
translations.idiomatic: South of Xu no city still stood firm.

sentences.zh: 有奸人素通賊，倡言城小宜速降，振之怒叱退之。

translations.literal: There was a wicked man who had long communicated with the bandits and advocated that the city was small and ought to surrender quickly; Zhenzhi angrily rebuked him and drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: A traitor who had long dealt with the rebels urged that the small city should surrender at once; Zhenzhi rebuked him and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 典史杜邦舉曰：「城存與存，亡與亡，人臣大義，公言是。」

translations.literal: Registrar Du Bangju said: "If the city survives we survive; if it perishes we perish—this is the great duty of a minister; what you say is right.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Du Bangju said, "If the city stands we stand; if it falls we fall—that is a minister's great duty, and you are right.

sentences.zh: 振之乃與集吏民共守。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi then gathered clerks and people to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi then rallied clerks and townspeople to defend together.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，城陷，振之秉笏坐堂上。

translations.literal: The bandits came in force; the city fell; Zhenzhi sat in the hall holding his tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came in force; the city fell; Zhenzhi sat in the hall with his tablet in hand.

sentences.zh: 賊索印，不與，縛置雪中三日夜，罵不絕口，亂刃交下乃死。

translations.literal: The bandits demanded the seal; he would not give it; they bound him and set him in the snow for three days and nights; he cursed without cease; only when blades struck from all sides did he die.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded the seal; he refused; they bound him in the snow for three days and nights, cursing without pause, until blades struck from every side and he died.

sentences.zh: 初，振之書一小簡，藏篋中，每歲元旦取視，輒加紙封其上。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhenzhi had written a small slip and kept it in a box; every New Year's Day he took it out to look at it and added another paper seal on top.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had written a small slip and kept it in a box; each New Year he opened it and added another paper seal.

sentences.zh: 及死，家人發篋，乃「不貪財、不好色、不畏死」三語也，其立誌如此。

translations.literal: When he died his family opened the box; it contained three phrases: "Do not covet wealth, do not lust, do not fear death"—such was the resolve he had set.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the family opened the box and found three lines: "Do not covet wealth, do not lust, do not fear death"—such was the pledge he had kept.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 邦舉，富平人。

translations.literal: Bangju was a native of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Bangju was from Fuping.

sentences.zh: 許被屠，鄢陵人恟懼，守者或遁走，邦舉捕得，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Xu was massacred; the people of Yanling were terrified; some defenders fled; Bangju seized them and executed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu was slaughtered Yanling panicked; some defenders fled; Bangju caught them and executed them as a warning.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，自成欲降之，邦舉罵曰：「朝廷臣子，豈為賊用！」

translations.literal: When the city fell Zicheng wished to induce his surrender; Bangju cursed: "A minister and subject of the court—how could I serve bandits!
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Zicheng tried to win him over; Bangju cried, "A subject of the dynasty—how could I serve rebels!

sentences.zh: 賊抉其舌，含血噴之，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The bandits cut out his tongue; he spat blood at them and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels cut out his tongue; he spat blood at them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 開封屬邑多陷，殉難者，有費曾謀、魏令望、柴薦禋、楊一鵬、劉孔暉、王化行、姚文衡之屬。

translations.literal: Many subordinate counties of Kaifeng had fallen; among those who died for the state were Fei Zengmou, Wei Lingwang, Chai Jianyin, Yang Yipeng, Liu Konghui, Wang Huaxing, Yao Wenheng, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Many Kaifeng subordinate counties had fallen; among those who died for the state were Fei Zengmou, Wei Lingwang, Chai Jianyin, Yang Yipeng, Liu Konghui, Wang Huaxing, Yao Wenheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 曾謀，鉛山人，少師宏裔也。

translations.literal: Zengmou was a native of Qianshan and grandson of Junior Tutor Fei Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zengmou was from Qianshan and grandson of Junior Tutor Fei Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉知通許，甫四旬，賊猝至。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he became magistrate of Tongxu; barely forty days in office, the bandits suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Tongxu through the provincial examination; barely forty days later the rebels struck.

sentences.zh: 曾謀召父老曰：「我死，若輩以城降，可免屠戮。」

translations.literal: Zengmou summoned the elders and said: "When I die, you may surrender the city and avoid massacre.
translations.idiomatic: Zengmou called the elders and said, "When I am dead, you may surrender the city and be spared massacre.

sentences.zh: 北向再拜，抱印投井死。

translations.literal: He bowed twice toward the north, embraced the seal, and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice to the north, clasped the seal, and threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 令望，字於野，武鄉人。

translations.literal: Lingwang, courtesy name Yuye, was a native of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwang, style name Yuye, was from Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授商丘知縣，調太康。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate of Shangqiu, then transferred to Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination, became magistrate of Shangqiu, then was transferred to Taikang.

sentences.zh: 寇至，固守不下。

translations.literal: When bandits came he held firm and they could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came he held firm and they could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，攻破之，屠其城，令望闔門自焚。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger broke through, slaughtered the city, and Lingwang burned himself together with his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels stormed in, massacred the city, and Lingwang burned himself with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 薦禋，江山舉人，知洧川，城陷，大罵死。

translations.literal: Jianyin, a provincial graduate of Jiangshan, was magistrate of Weichuan; when the city fell he cursed loudly and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyin, a Jiangshan provincial graduate, was magistrate of Weichuan; when the city fell he reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 一鵬，河津人。

translations.literal: Yipeng was a native of Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng was from Hejin.

sentences.zh: 舉崇禎九年鄉試，為尉氏知縣，甫數月，政聲四起。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the ninth year of Chongzhen and became magistrate of Weishi; within a few months his reputation for good government spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Chongzhen year nine and became magistrate of Weishi; within months his reputation for good government rang out on every side.

sentences.zh: 城破，罵賊死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 孔暉，邵陽人。

translations.literal: Konghui was a native of Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Konghui was from Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟元年鄉試，知新鄭，固守不能支，遂死之。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Tianqi, became magistrate of Xinzheng, held firm but could not sustain it, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Tianqi year one, became magistrate of Xinzheng, held out but could not endure, and died.

sentences.zh: 士民祀之子產祠。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners worshipped him in the Temple of Zichan.
translations.idiomatic: The people enshrined him in the Temple of Zichan.

sentences.zh: 化行，知商水，城陷，被殺。

translations.literal: Huaxing was magistrate of Shangshui; when the city fell he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxing was magistrate of Shangshui; when the city fell he was killed.

sentences.zh: 代者文衡，蒞任數月，賊復至，攜印赴井死。

translations.literal: His successor Wenheng had been in office only a few months when the bandits came again; he took the seal and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His successor Wenheng had served only a few months when the rebels returned; he took the seal and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 其小吏，則臨潁千總賈蔭序、長葛典史杜復春，鄉居則長葛舉人孟良屏、諸生張範孔等，汜水舉人張治載、馬德茂，皆死之。

translations.literal: Among the minor officials, Battalion Commander Jia Yinxu of Linying and Registrar Du Fuchun of Changge died; among those living locally, Changge graduate Meng Liangping, students Zhang Fankong and others, and Sishui graduates Zhang Zhizai and Ma Demao all died.
translations.idiomatic: Minor officials included Linying battalion commander Jia Yinxu and Changge registrar Du Fuchun; local men included Changge graduate Meng Liangping, students Zhang Fankong and others, and Sishui graduates Zhang Zhizai and Ma Demao—all died.

sentences.zh: 李乘雲，高陽人，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Li Chengyun was a native of Gaoyang and had passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengyun was from Gaoyang and had passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，知浮山縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was magistrate of Fushan County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was magistrate of Fushan.

sentences.zh: 流賊數萬來寇，乘雲手發一矢斃其魁，眾遂遁。

translations.literal: When tens of thousands of roving bandits came to attack, Chengyun with his own hand shot one arrow and killed their chief; the host then fled.
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of roving rebels attacked, Chengyun shot one arrow himself and killed their leader; the host fled.

sentences.zh: 屢遷山西僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Shanxi Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Shanxi Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，以才調河南大梁道，駐禹州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, for his ability he was transferred to the Daliang Circuit in Henan and stationed at Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year fourteen he was transferred for merit to the Daliang circuit in Henan and stationed at Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李自成連陷鄢陵、陳留諸縣，遂寇禹州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Li Zicheng in succession took Yanling, Chenliu, and other counties, then came to raid Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Zicheng seized Yanling, Chenliu, and other counties in turn, then marched on Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乘雲誓死固守，賊多斃於炮。

translations.literal: Chengyun swore to die in a stubborn defense; many bandits were killed by cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyun vowed to die defending the city; many rebels fell to cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 俄以十萬眾攀堞登，執乘雲使跪，乘雲怒叱賊，賊捽而杖之，大罵不絕聲。

translations.literal: Soon a host of a hundred thousand scaled the battlements; they seized Chengyun and made him kneel; Chengyun angrily rebuked the bandits; they dragged him down and beat him with sticks; he cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a hundred thousand men climbed the walls; they seized Chengyun and forced him to kneel; he reviled them; they dragged him down and beat him, cursing without pause.

sentences.zh: 縛諸樹攢射之，罵不已，斷其舌，亂刃交下而死。

translations.literal: They bound him to a tree and shot at him in a crowd; he still cursed; they cut out his tongue; blades struck from all sides and he died.
translations.idiomatic: They bound him to a tree and shot him in a crowd; he still cursed; they cut out his tongue; blades struck from every side and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 州先有徽王府，嘉靖時，王載埨有罪，爵絕，而延津等五郡王皆被難。

translations.literal: The prefecture had formerly had a Huai princely establishment; in the Jiajing era Prince Zaijun committed an offense and the title lapsed, while the five commandery princes of Yanjin and others all suffered in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou had once held a Huai princely establishment; in Jiajing Prince Zaijun offended and the line ended, while five commandery princes including Yanjin all perished in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊犯開封，監軍主事余爵、監軍僉事任棟先後戰死。

translations.literal: The following year the bandits attacked Kaifeng; Supervising Secretary Yu Jue and Supervising Assistant Commissioner Ren Dong died in battle in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels attacked Kaifeng; Supervising Secretary Yu Jue and Supervising Assistant Commissioner Ren Dong died in battle one after another.

sentences.zh: 棟，永壽人，由貢生為萊州通判。

translations.literal: Dong was a native of Yongshou and had entered office through the tribute-student route as Vice Prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was from Yongshou and had become vice prefect of Laizhou through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，李九成等叛，棟佐知府朱萬年共守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen Li Jiucheng and others rebelled; Dong assisted Prefect Zhu Wannian in joint defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year four Li Jiucheng and others rebelled; Dong helped Prefect Zhu Wannian hold the city.

sentences.zh: 萬年與巡撫謝璉為賊所誘執，棟與同知寇化、掖縣知縣洪恩炤助大帥楊禦蕃力拒。

translations.literal: Wannian and Governor Xie Lian were lured out and seized by the bandits; Dong, together with Vice Magistrate Kou Hua and Yexian Magistrate Hong Enzhao, assisted Commander Yang Yufan in strenuous resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian and Governor Xie Lian were lured out and captured; Dong, with Vice Magistrate Kou Hua and Yexian Magistrate Hong Enzhao, helped Commander Yang Yufan resist fiercely.

sentences.zh: 圍解，論功進秩，屢遷保定監軍僉事。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted merit was assessed for promotion; he was repeatedly transferred to Baoding Supervising Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege lifted he was promoted for merit and eventually became Baoding supervising assistant commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十四年從總督楊文嶽南征，鳴臯鎮之捷，與有功。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed Governor-General Yang Wenyue on the southern campaign; at the victory at Minggao Town he had a share in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he followed Governor-General Yang Wenyue south and shared in the victory at Minggao Town.

sentences.zh: 尋與總兵虎大威破賊平峪，再破之鄧州。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Regional Commander Hu Dawei in defeating the bandits at Pingyu and again at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Regional Commander Hu Dawei in defeating the rebels at Pingyu and again at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，從解開封圍。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he joined in relieving the siege of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he helped lift the siege of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 尋戰郾城，大捷。

translations.literal: Soon he fought at Yancheng and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fought at Yancheng and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 後從援開封，會左良玉大潰於朱仙鎮，賊來追，棟力戰，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Later he followed the relief of Kaifeng; just then Zuo Liangyu suffered a great rout at Zhuxian Town; the bandits pursued; Dong fought hard and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Later he marched to relieve Kaifeng; Zuo Liangyu was routed at Zhuxian Town; the rebels pursued; Dong fought hard and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 余爵，禹州人。

translations.literal: Yu Jue was a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jue was from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year one.

sentences.zh: 歷知撫寧、章丘。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Funing and Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Funing and Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 遷職方主事，罷歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War and then dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of War, then was dismissed and went home.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌出督師，請爵以故官參謀軍事。

translations.literal: When Yang Sichang went out as supervising commander he asked that Jue, in his former office, serve on the staff as military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang took command he asked that Jue serve on his staff in his former post.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌入蜀，命與張克儉同守襄陽。

translations.literal: When Sichang entered Shu he ordered Jue and Zhang Kejian to guard Xiangyang together.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang entered Shu he ordered Jue and Zhang Kejian to guard Xiangyang together.

sentences.zh: 城陷，爵脫走，從督師丁啟睿於河南，破賊鄧州。

translations.literal: When the city fell Jue escaped; he followed Supervising Commander Ding Qirui in Henan and defeated the bandits at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang fell Jue escaped; he followed Supervising Commander Ding Qirui in Henan and defeated the rebels at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，開封圍急，監左良玉軍往援，戰敗被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the siege of Kaifeng was urgent; he supervised Zuo Liangyu's army to relieve it; he was defeated in battle, seized, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Kaifeng was hard pressed; he supervised Zuo Liangyu's relief army, was defeated, captured, reviled the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 侄敦華亦遇害。

translations.literal: His nephew Dunhua was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Dunhua was also killed.

sentences.zh: 棟贈太僕卿，爵太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Dong was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Stud; Jue, Junior Director of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was posthumously made Grand Master of the Stud; Jue, Junior Director of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 關永傑，字人孟，鞏昌衛人。

translations.literal: Guan Yongjie, courtesy name Renmeng, was a native of Gongchang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yongjie, style name Renmeng, was from Gongchang Guard.

sentences.zh: 世官百戶。

translations.literal: His family held a hereditary centurion post.
translations.idiomatic: His family held a hereditary centurion post.

sentences.zh: 永傑好讀書，每遇忠義事，輒書之壁。

translations.literal: Yongjie loved reading; whenever he encountered a story of loyalty and righteousness he would write it on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjie loved books; whenever he met a tale of loyalty and righteousness he wrote it on the wall.

sentences.zh: 狀貌奇偉，類世人所繪壯繆侯像。

translations.literal: His appearance was remarkably imposing, resembling the painted image of the Marquis Zhuang that people commonly depict.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in bearing, like the painted image of Marquis Zhuang that people commonly worship.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年會試入都，與儕輩遊壯繆祠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he entered the capital for the metropolitan examination and with his companions visited the Marquis Zhuang temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year four he came to the capital for the metropolitan examination and visited the Marquis Zhuang temple with his companions.

sentences.zh: 有道士前曰：「昨夢神告：『吾後人當有登第者，後且繼我忠義，可語之。』」

translations.literal: A Daoist priest came forward and said: "Last night I dreamed the god told me: 'Among my descendants one will pass the examination; later he will follow my loyalty and righteousness—you may tell him.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist came forward and said, "Last night I dreamed the god said, 'Among my descendants one will pass the examination and later follow my loyalty—you may tell him.

sentences.zh: 永傑愕然，頗自喜。

translations.literal: Yongjie was startled and rather pleased with himself.'
translations.idiomatic: Yongjie was startled and rather pleased.'

sentences.zh: 已果登第，授開封推官，強植不阿，民畏愛之。

translations.literal: He did indeed pass the examination and was appointed investigating censor of Kaifeng; upright and unyielding, the people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He did pass the examination and became investigating censor of Kaifeng; upright and unbending, the people feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，起官紹興。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning and then took office in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for mourning, then took office in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部主事，督師楊嗣昌薦其才，請用之軍前，乃擢睢陳兵備僉事，駐陳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War; Supervising Commander Yang Sichang recommended his talent and asked to use him at the front; he was then promoted to Suichen Military Vice Commissioner and stationed at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of War; Yang Sichang recommended his talent for the front; he was promoted to Suichen military vice commissioner and stationed at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳故賊沖，歲被蹂躪，永傑日夜為儆備。

translations.literal: Chen was formerly a bandit thoroughfare and was ravaged year after year; Yongjie made preparations day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had long been a rebel corridor and was ravaged yearly; Yongjie prepared day and night.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，李自成數十萬眾來攻，永傑與知州侯君擢、鄉官崔泌之、舉人王受爵等率士民分堞守。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Li Zicheng came to attack with several hundred thousand men; Yongjie together with Prefect Hou Junzhuo, local elder Cui Mizhi, graduate Wang Shoujue, and others led gentry and commoners to defend section by section along the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year fifteen Li Zicheng attacked with hundreds of thousands; Yongjie, Prefect Hou Junzhuo, local elder Cui Mizhi, graduate Wang Shoujue, and others led townspeople to hold each section of the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊遣使說降，斬其頭，懸之城上。

translations.literal: The bandits sent envoys to induce surrender; he cut off their heads and hung them on the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent envoys to negotiate surrender; he cut off their heads and hung them on the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，攻破之，永傑格殺數賊，身中亂刃而死。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger broke through; Yongjie killed several bandits in close combat and died under a rain of blades.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels stormed in; Yongjie killed several in close combat and died under many blades.

sentences.zh: 君擢，字際明，成安人，起家舉人。

translations.literal: Junzhuo, courtesy name Jiming, was a native of Cheng'an and had begun his career as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhuo, style name Jiming, was from Cheng'an and had entered office through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 城圍時，身先士卒，運木石擊賊，城濠皆滿。

translations.literal: During the siege he led the troops in person, hauled wood and stone to strike the bandits, and filled the moat completely.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege he led from the front, hauled wood and stone against the rebels, and filled the moat.

sentences.zh: 後被縛，罵不絕口死。

translations.literal: Later he was bound and died cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was bound and died still cursing.

sentences.zh: 泌之，鹿邑人。

translations.literal: Mizhi was a native of Luyi.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi was from Luyi.

sentences.zh: 進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 知雄縣，調清苑，多所建豎。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Xiong County, transferred to Qingyuan, and accomplished much in his administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was magistrate of Xiong County, then Qingyuan, and built much in his administration.

sentences.zh: 舊令黃宗昌為御史，劾周延儒，延儒屬保定知府摭宗昌罪。

translations.literal: The former magistrate Huang Zongchang had been a censor and impeached Zhou Yanru; Yanru had the Baoding prefect gather charges against Zongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The former magistrate Huang Zongchang had been a censor and impeached Zhou Yanru; Yanru had the Baoding prefect fabricate charges against him.

sentences.zh: 知府以屬泌之，泌之曰：「殺人媚人可乎！」

translations.literal: The prefect assigned the matter to Mizhi; Mizhi said: "Is it permissible to kill people to please others!
translations.idiomatic: The prefect put the case to Mizhi; Mizhi said, "Is it right to kill a man to please another?

sentences.zh: 知府愧且怒。

translations.literal: The prefect was ashamed and also angry.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was ashamed and furious.

sentences.zh: 會泌之遷戶部主事，知府謂其侵陷錢糧三萬，不聽行。

translations.literal: Just as Mizhi was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, the prefect accused him of embezzling thirty thousand in taxes and grain and would not let him depart.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Mizhi was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, the prefect accused him of embezzling thirty thousand in revenue and blocked his departure.

sentences.zh: 御史行部至，泌之直前與知府角。

translations.literal: When a touring censor arrived Mizhi went straight forward and argued with the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When a touring censor arrived Mizhi confronted the prefect openly.

sentences.zh: 御史以聞，下獄遣戍，久之釋還。

translations.literal: The censor reported it; Mizhi was imprisoned and sent into exile; after a long time he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The censor reported it; Mizhi was jailed and exiled; long afterward he was released.

sentences.zh: 至是，遭變，用鐵杖斃賊數人，自剄死。

translations.literal: On this occasion when disaster struck he used an iron staff to kill several bandits and then cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster came he killed several rebels with an iron staff, then cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 守備張鷹揚力戰被擒，不屈。

translations.literal: Garrison Commander Zhang Yingyang fought hard, was captured, and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Zhang Yingyang fought fiercely, was taken, and would not submit.

sentences.zh: 受爵亦擊殺數賊，大罵。

translations.literal: Shoujue also struck and killed several bandits and cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujue also killed several rebels and reviled them.

sentences.zh: 並死之。

translations.literal: All died.
translations.idiomatic: They all died.

sentences.zh: 贈永傑光祿卿，君擢右參議，泌之復故官。

translations.literal: Yongjie was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Junzhuo, Right Assistant Commissioner; Mizhi was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjie was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Junzhuo, Right Assistant Commissioner; Mizhi was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 受爵，宛平知縣。

translations.literal: Shoujue was magistrate of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujue was magistrate of Wanping.

sentences.zh: 有龔作梅者，年十七，父母俱亡，殯於舍。

translations.literal: There was a Gong Zuomei, seventeen years old; both parents were dead and lay in coffins in the house.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Gong Zuomei, seventeen; both parents were dead and lay in coffins at home.

sentences.zh: 賊火民居，作梅跪柩前焚死。

translations.literal: The bandits set fire to civilian houses; Zuomei knelt before the coffins and was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels torched houses; Zuomei knelt before the coffins and burned to death.

sentences.zh: 張維世，太康人。

translations.literal: Zhang Weishi was a native of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Weishi was from Taikang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Wanli year forty-four.

sentences.zh: 歷平陽知府，捕治絳州奸猾數十人，遷副使。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Pingyang, captured and punished several dozen crafty villains of Jiangzhou, and was transferred to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was prefect of Pingyang, seized dozens of Jiangzhou scoundrels, and was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累官右僉都御史，代陳新甲巡撫宣府，視事甫旬日，坐失防，削籍遣戍，已而釋還。

translations.literal: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, replaced Chen Xinji as Governor of Xuanfu; he had been in office only ten days when he was punished for a failure of defense, stripped of rank and sent into exile, and later released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and replaced Chen Xinji as Xuanfu governor; ten days into office he was punished for defensive failure, stripped and exiled, then later released.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年二月，李自成陷睢州，犯太康。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen Li Zicheng took Suizhou and invaded Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chongzhen year fifteen Li Zicheng took Suizhou and invaded Taikang.

sentences.zh: 維世佐知縣魏令望竭力拒守。

translations.literal: Weishi assisted Magistrate Wei Lingwang in strenuous resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi helped Magistrate Wei Lingwang hold the city with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 城陷，抗節死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he died holding to his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he died holding his integrity.

sentences.zh: 時中州縉紳先後死難者甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time many gentry of the central plain died for the state in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Many central-plain gentry died for the state in succession.

sentences.zh: 十三年，登封土寇李際遇因歲饑倡亂，旬日間眾數萬。
