translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Dengfeng local bandit Li Jiyu, taking advantage of famine, raised rebellion; within ten days his host numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen the Dengfeng bandit Li Jiyu, exploiting famine, raised rebellion; within ten days he had tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 前鳳陽通判姚若時居魯莊，被執，誘之降，大罵死。

translations.literal: Former Fengyang Vice Prefect Yao Ruoshi lived at Luzhuang; he was seized and induced to surrender; he cursed loudly and died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Fengyang vice prefect Yao Ruoshi lived at Luzhuang; seized and urged to surrender, he reviled them and died.

sentences.zh: 族諸生不顯亦死之。

translations.literal: His clansman the student Bu Xian also died.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman the student Bu Xian died as well.

sentences.zh: 若時子諸生城，思報父仇，數請兵討賊。

translations.literal: Ruoshi's son the student Cheng, thinking to avenge his father, repeatedly asked for troops to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshi's son Cheng, burning to avenge his father, repeatedly begged for troops.

sentences.zh: 賊執之於路，亦抗罵死。

translations.literal: The bandits seized him on the road; he too resisted and cursed and died.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized him on the road; he too resisted, reviled them, and died.

sentences.zh: 陜州趙良棟，仕蓬萊教諭，罷歸，寓澠池。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangdong of Shanzhou had served as instructor of Penglai, retired, and was staying at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangdong of Shanzhou had been Penglai instructor, retired, and lodged at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 寇陷澠池，父子挺身罵賊死，子婦與孫亦赴井以殉。

translations.literal: When bandits took Mianchi, father and son stepped forward together, cursed the bandits, and died; the son's wife and grandson also entered a well in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Mianchi fell father and son cursed the rebels and died; the son's wife and grandson entered a well in martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 陜州之陷，平定知州梁可棟大罵而死，淮安同知萬大成投井死。

translations.literal: When Shanzhou fell, Pingding Magistrate Liang Kedong cursed loudly and died; Huai'an Vice Prefect Wan Dacheng threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanzhou fell Pingding magistrate Liang Kedong reviled them and died; Huai'an vice prefect Wan Dacheng drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 商水陷，臨汾知縣張質抗賊死。

translations.literal: When Shangshui fell, Linfen Magistrate Zhang Zhi resisted the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangshui fell Linfen magistrate Zhang Zhi resisted and died.

sentences.zh: 西平陷，懷仁知縣楊士英死之，子婦王亦死。

translations.literal: When Xiping fell, Huairen Magistrate Yang Shiying died, and his son's wife Wang also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiping fell Huairen magistrate Yang Shiying died, and his daughter-in-law Wang as well.

sentences.zh: 睢州陷，太平知府杜時髦不屈死。

translations.literal: When Suizhou fell, Taiping Prefect Du Shimao refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Suizhou fell Taiping prefect Du Shimao refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 時髦，字觀生，崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: Shimao, courtesy name Guansheng, was a metropolitan graduate in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shimao, style name Guansheng, was a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year seven.

sentences.zh: 息縣陷，賊召前項城教諭王多福欲官之，堅拒不赴。

translations.literal: When Xi County fell the bandits summoned the former Xiangcheng Instructor Wang Duofu and wished to give him office; he firmly refused and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi County fell the rebels summoned former Xiangcheng instructor Wang Duofu for office; he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 賊逼之，投繯死。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed him; he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him; he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 其後以國變死者，有洛陽阮泰，知廣靈，解職歸。

translations.literal: Later those who died because of the dynastic collapse included Ruan Tai of Luoyang, who had been magistrate of Guangling and returned home after leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Later those who died from the dynastic collapse included Ruan Tai of Luoyang, former magistrate of Guangling, home after leaving office.

sentences.zh: 聞京師陷，不食死，妻朱氏從之。

translations.literal: When he heard the capital had fallen he stopped eating and died; his wife the Lady Zhu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the capital had fallen he stopped eating and died; his wife Lady Zhu followed.

sentences.zh: 睢州楊汝經，崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: Yang Rujing of Suizhou was a metropolitan graduate in the tenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rujing of Suizhou was a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year ten.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，擢井陘兵備僉事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to Jingxing Military Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became director in the Ministry of Revenue, then Jingxing military vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十七年，甘肅陷，巡撫林日瑞殉難，超拜汝經右僉都御史，代之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Gansu fell; Governor Lin Rirui died for the state; Rujing was promoted over the regular order to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen Gansu fell; Governor Lin Rirui died; Rujing was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him.

sentences.zh: 行次林縣，聞京師陷，將赴南京，至東明，率壯士百余騎還討林縣偽官。

translations.literal: Stopping at Lin County he heard the capital had fallen and was about to go to Nanjing; reaching Dongming he led more than a hundred stalwart horsemen back to attack the false officials of Lin County.
translations.idiomatic: At Lin County he heard the capital had fallen and set out for Nanjing; at Dongming he led a hundred stalwart horsemen back against Lin County's puppet officials.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，戰敗被執。

translations.literal: He met bandits, was defeated in battle, and seized.
translations.idiomatic: He met rebels, was defeated, and captured.

sentences.zh: 偽官釋其縛，屢說之降，不從，斃之獄。

translations.literal: The false officials released his bonds and repeatedly urged him to surrender; he would not obey and was beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet officials freed his bonds and urged surrender again and again; he refused and was beaten to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 王世琇，字昆良，清苑人。

translations.literal: Wang Shixiu, courtesy name Kunliang, was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixiu, style name Kunliang, was from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Chongzhen year ten.

sentences.zh: 授歸德推官，遷工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Guide and transferred to Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was investigating censor of Guide, then director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，李自成陷陳州，乘勝犯歸德。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Li Zicheng took Chenzhou and, pressing his advantage, invaded Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year fifteen Li Zicheng took Chenzhou and pressed on to Guide.

sentences.zh: 世琇將行，僚屬邀共守，慨然曰：「久官其地，臨難而去之，非誼也。」

translations.literal: Shixiu was about to depart; his colleagues invited him to defend together; he said with emotion: "I have long served this place; to leave when disaster comes is not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was leaving; colleagues asked him to stay and defend; he said, "I have served here long—to flee in crisis is not righteous.

sentences.zh: 遂與同知顏則孔、經歷徐一源、商丘知縣梁以樟、教諭夏世英、裏居尚書周士樸等誓眾堅守。

translations.literal: He then together with Vice Magistrate Yan Zekong, Administrator Xu Yiyuan, Shangqiu Magistrate Liang Yizhang, Instructor Xia Shiying, and retired Minister Zhou Shipu and others swore the crowd to a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Vice Magistrate Yan Zekong, Administrator Xu Yiyuan, Shangqiu Magistrate Liang Yizhang, Instructor Xia Shiying, retired Minister Zhou Shipu, and others in swearing the people to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 賊攻圍七日，總督侯恂家商丘，其子方夏率家眾斬關出，傷守者，眾遂亂。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged for seven days; Governor Hou Xun's family was in Shangqiu; his son Fangxia led the household retainers to cut through the gate and go out, wounding the defenders, and the crowd fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged seven days; Governor Hou Xun's household was in Shangqiu; his son Fangxia cut through the gate with family troops, wounded defenders, and the line broke.

sentences.zh: 賊乘之入，世琇、則孔並遇害。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the opportunity to enter; Shixiu and Zekong were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels poured in; Shixiu and Zekong were both killed.

sentences.zh: 則孔女聞之，即自縊。

translations.literal: When Zekong's daughter heard it she immediately hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Zekong's daughter hanged herself on hearing it.

sentences.zh: 一源分守北城，殺賊多，城陷，巷戰，罵賊死。

translations.literal: Yiyuan held divided defense at the north wall, killed many bandits; when the city fell he fought in the lanes, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan held the north wall, killed many rebels; when the city fell he fought in the alleys, reviled them, and died.

sentences.zh: 以樟中賊刃，久而復蘇，妻張及子女仆從皆死，以樟竟獲免。

translations.literal: Yizhang was struck by a bandit blade; after a long time he revived; his wife Zhang and children and servants all died, but Yizhang ultimately escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang took a rebel blade and long lay senseless; his wife Zhang, children, and servants all died, yet he survived.

sentences.zh: 世英持刀罵賊，死於明倫堂，妻石亦自刎。

translations.literal: Shiying took a knife and cursed the bandits; he died in the Hall of Bright Moral Teaching; his wife Shi also cut her own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying seized a knife and reviled the rebels; he died in the Hall of Bright Moral Teaching; his wife Shi cut her throat.

sentences.zh: 同死者，尚書士樸，工部郎中沈試，主事朱國慶，中書侯忻，廣西知府沈仔，威縣知縣張儒及舉人徐作霖、吳伯胤、周士美等六人，官生沈佖、侯矣等三人，貢生侯恒、沈誠、周士貴等八人，國學生侯悰、沈倜等四人，諸生吳伯裔、張渭、劉伯愚等一百十余人。

translations.literal: Those who died together included Minister Shipu, Director in the Ministry of Works Shen Shi, Director Zhu Guoqing, Secretariat Drafter Hou Xin, Guangxi Prefect Shen Zai, Weixian Magistrate Zhang Ru, and graduates Xu Zuolin, Wu Boyin, Zhou Shimei and six others; official students Shen Yi, Hou Yi and three others; tribute students Hou Heng, Shen Cheng, Zhou Shigui and eight others; Imperial Academy students Hou Cong, Shen Tong and four others; and students Wu Boyi, Zhang Wei, Liu Boxian and more than a hundred and ten others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with them included Minister Shipu, Works director Shen Shi, director Zhu Guoqing, drafter Hou Xin, Guangxi prefect Shen Zai, Weixian magistrate Zhang Ru, graduates Xu Zuolin, Wu Boyin, Zhou Shimei and six others, official students Shen Yi and Hou Yi and three more, tribute students Hou Heng, Shen Cheng, Zhou Shigui and eight others, academy students Hou Cong and Shen Tong and four more, and students Wu Boyi, Zhang Wei, Liu Boxian and more than a hundred and ten besides.

sentences.zh: 試，商丘人，大學士鯉之孫。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Shangqiu and grandson of Grand Secretary Li.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was from Shangqiu and grandson of Grand Secretary Li.

sentences.zh: 作霖、伯胤、伯裔、渭、伯愚，皆郡中名士。

translations.literal: Zuolin, Boyin, Boyi, Wei, and Boxian were all celebrated men of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zuolin, Boyin, Boyi, Wei, and Boxian were all famed men of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則孔，忻州人。

translations.literal: Zekong was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zekong was from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 一源，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Yiyuan was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan was from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 世英，祥符人。

translations.literal: Shiying was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 士樸自有傳。

translations.literal: Shipu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 賊既破歸德，尋陷鹿邑，知縣紀懋勛死之。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had broken Guide they soon took Luyi; Magistrate Ji Maoxun died.
translations.idiomatic: After Guide fell they soon took Luyi; Magistrate Ji Maoxun died.

sentences.zh: 陷虞城，署縣事主簿孔亮死之。

translations.literal: They took Yucheng; Acting Magistrate Kong Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: They took Yucheng; acting magistrate Kong Liang died.

sentences.zh: 許永禧，曲沃人。

translations.literal: Xu Yongxi was a native of Quwo.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yongxi was from Quwo.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉為上蔡知縣，多惠政。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he became magistrate of Shangcai and had many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Shangcai through the provincial examination and ruled with many humane policies.

sentences.zh: 性耿介，嚬笑無所假。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and unyielding; he never smiled or laughed without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and unyielding by nature, he never smiled without reason.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年春，李自成遣數騎抵城下，脅降，永禧即督吏民城守。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen Li Zicheng sent several horsemen to the foot of the wall to coerce surrender; Yongxi immediately supervised clerks and people in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fifteen Li Zicheng sent horsemen to the wall to demand surrender; Yongxi at once rallied clerks and people to defend.

sentences.zh: 賊大呼曰：「今日不降，明日屠！」

translations.literal: The bandits shouted loudly: "If you do not surrender today, tomorrow we slaughter!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shouted, "Surrender today or we slaughter tomorrow!

sentences.zh: 眾懼，永禧嘆曰：「賊勢披猖，彈丸邑豈能守，吾一死盡職而已！」

translations.literal: The crowd was afraid; Yongxi sighed and said: "The bandits' power runs wild; how can a tiny county hold out—I shall die in fulfillment of duty, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: The people panicked; Yongxi sighed, "The rebels run riot—how can this tiny county hold? I can only die doing my duty!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊果大至，守者驚潰。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits indeed came in force; the defenders panicked and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the rebels came in force; the defenders broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 永禧具袍笏，北面再拜，據案秉燭端坐。

translations.literal: Yongxi put on robe and hat, bowed twice toward the north, and sat upright at his desk holding a candle.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi donned robe and hat, bowed twice north, and sat upright at his desk with a candle.

sentences.zh: 賊入，遂自剄。

translations.literal: When the bandits entered he cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered he cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 時西平、遂平先後皆陷。

translations.literal: At that time Xiping and Suiping had both fallen in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping and Suiping had both fallen in turn.

sentences.zh: 西平知縣高鬥垣，繁峙人。

translations.literal: Douyuan, magistrate of Xiping, was a native of Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Douyuan, magistrate of Xiping, was from Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十二年由貢生授官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen he received office through the tribute-student route.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year twelve he entered office through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 為人孤鯁，以清慎得名。

translations.literal: He was solitary and stern in character and was famed for integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary and stern, he was famed for integrity and caution.

sentences.zh: 城陷，被執不屈死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized and died refusing to yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was seized and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 遂平知縣劉英，貴州貢生，誓眾死守。

translations.literal: Liu Ying, magistrate of Suiping, was a Guizhou tribute student and swore the crowd to die in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ying, Suiping magistrate, was a Guizhou tribute student and swore the people to die defending.

sentences.zh: 城陷，罵賊死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 上蔡既陷，有官篆者，以汝寧通判往攝縣事。

translations.literal: After Shangcai had fallen there was an official named Zuan who went as Runan Vice Prefect to take charge of county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shangcai fell an official named Zuan went as Runan vice prefect to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 城中民舍盡毀，篆廣招流亡，眾觀望不敢入。

translations.literal: Civilian houses in the city were all destroyed; Zuan widely summoned the displaced, but the people watched hesitantly and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The town was ruined; Zuan called back the displaced, but people hesitated to return.

sentences.zh: 會左良玉駐城南，兵士恣淫掠，眾始入城依篆。

translations.literal: Just then Zuo Liangyu was stationed south of the city and his soldiers wantonly raped and plundered; only then did the people enter the city and rely on Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu camped south of the city and his men raped and plundered; only then did people enter and shelter under Zuan.

sentences.zh: 村民遭難來訴，篆即入良玉營，責以大義，奪還之。

translations.literal: Villagers who had suffered came to complain; Zuan at once entered Liangyu's camp, rebuked him with the great principles of duty, and recovered them.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers came pleading; Zuan entered Liangyu's camp, rebuked him on duty, and recovered them.

sentences.zh: 悍卒挾弓刃相向，篆坦腹當之，不敢害，民獲完家室者甚眾。

translations.literal: Fierce soldiers confronted him with bow and blade; Zuan bared his belly to them and they did not dare harm him; many people thus preserved their households.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce soldiers leveled bows and blades at him; Zuan bared his breast and they dared not harm him; many families were saved.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，汝寧陷，賊黨賀一龍掠地上蔡。

translations.literal: That winter Runan fell; the bandit partisan He Yilong raided the Shangcai region.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Runan fell; rebel ally He Yilong raided Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 訛傳土寇剽掠，篆出禦之，陷陣死。

translations.literal: A false report said local bandits were plundering; Zuan went out to meet them and died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: A false alarm said local bandits were raiding; Zuan rode out and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 篆，膠州人，起家任子。

translations.literal: Zuan was a native of Jiaozhou and had begun his career as a hereditary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was from Jiaozhou and had begun as a hereditary clerk.

sentences.zh: 李貞佐，字無欲，安邑人。

translations.literal: Li Zhenzuo, courtesy name Wuyu, was a native of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhenzuo, style name Wuyu, was from Anyi.

sentences.zh: 少受業同里曹於汴之門，以學行著，後舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cao Yubian of the same district and was renowned for learning and conduct; later he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under his townsman Cao Yubian and was famed for learning and conduct; later he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年除知郟縣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Jia County.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year fourteen he became magistrate of Jia County.

sentences.zh: 初，李自成焚掠至郟，土寇導之，害前令邵可灼。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Zicheng had burned and plundered as far as Jia; local bandits guided them and killed the former magistrate Shao Kezhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Zicheng had raided Jia; local bandits guided him and killed former magistrate Shao Kezhuo.

sentences.zh: 貞佐至，則練鄉兵，括土寇財充餉，時出郊勞耕者，月課士。

translations.literal: When Zhenzuo arrived he drilled local militia, seized local bandit wealth to fill the commissariat, often went to the suburbs to encourage plowmen, and monthly examined the students.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzuo arrived he drilled militia, seized bandit wealth for supplies, encouraged farmers in the fields, and examined students monthly.

sentences.zh: 邑有姊妹二人抗賊死，拜其冢，祀以少牢。

translations.literal: In the district two sisters had resisted bandits and died; he bowed at their tombs and sacrificed with the secondary offering.
translations.idiomatic: Two sisters in the district had resisted rebels and died; he bowed at their tombs and sacrificed with the secondary offering.

sentences.zh: 民王錫胤有孝行，造廬禮之。

translations.literal: The commoner Wang Xiyin was filial; Zhenzuo built a lodge to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Wang Xiyin was filial; Zhenzuo built a lodge to honor him.

sentences.zh: 士民大悅。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，自成復來寇，貞佐集眾死守。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Zicheng came to attack again; Zhenzuo gathered the crowd to die in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Next second month Zicheng attacked again; Zhenzuo rallied the people to die defending.

sentences.zh: 汝州吏目顧王家，仁和人，撫賊有功，當遷，汝人乞留以助之。

translations.literal: Gu Wangjia, clerk of Ruzhou, a native of Renhe, had pacified bandits with merit and was due for transfer; the people of Ru begged that he be kept to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Wangjia, Ruzhou clerk from Renhe, had pacified rebels with merit and was due to transfer; the people of Ru begged he stay to help.

sentences.zh: 城陷，貞佐走拜其母曰：「兒不忠不孝，陷母至此。」

translations.literal: When the city fell Zhenzuo ran to bow to his mother and said: "Your son has been neither loyal nor filial and has brought mother to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Zhenzuo ran to his mother and said, "I have been neither loyal nor filial and brought you to this.

sentences.zh: 有勸微服遁者，不可，賊執之去，大罵。

translations.literal: Some urged him to flee in disguise; he would not; the bandits seized him and took him away; he cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee in disguise; he refused; the rebels seized him and he reviled them.

sentences.zh: 見賊殺人，輒厲聲曰：「驅百姓固守者，我也，妄殺何為！」

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the bandits killing people he would say in a stern voice: "It was I who drove the people to hold firm in defense—why kill them without cause!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw them kill he cried, "I drove the people to defend—why kill the innocent?

sentences.zh: 賊割其舌，支解而死，母喬亦死。

translations.literal: The bandits cut out his tongue and dismembered him; his mother Qiao also died.
translations.idiomatic: They cut out his tongue and cut him apart; his mother Qiao died as well.

sentences.zh: 友人王昱，相隨不去，賊義之。

translations.literal: His friend Wang Yu followed and would not leave; the bandits honored his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wang Yu would not leave; the rebels honored him.

sentences.zh: 昱收葬貞佐於南郊。

translations.literal: Yu gathered Zhenzuo's remains and buried him in the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu buried Zhenzuo in the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 歲寒食，鄉人傾邑祭奠，廣其冢至二畝余。

translations.literal: At the Cold Food Festival each year the people of the district turned out as one to sacrifice; they enlarged his mound to more than two mu.
translations.idiomatic: Each Cold Food Festival the whole district sacrificed; his mound was enlarged to more than two mu.

sentences.zh: 贈河南僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Henan Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Henan assistant commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王家亦大聲叱賊，賊亂刃斫死。

translations.literal: Wang Jia also rebuked the bandits loudly; the bandits hacked him to death with blades in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia also reviled the rebels; they hacked him to death.

sentences.zh: 子國誘賊發金墟墓間，用巨石擊殺之，賊遂盡殺郟人。

translations.literal: His son Guo lured the bandits to open the gold tombs between the mounds and used a great stone to strike and kill them; the bandits then slaughtered all the people of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo lured rebels to open tombs in the mounds and killed them with a great stone; the rebels then slaughtered everyone in Jia.

sentences.zh: 郟有陳心學者，授知縣，不謁選而歸。

translations.literal: In Jia there was Chen Xinxue, appointed magistrate but returned home without presenting himself for selection.
translations.idiomatic: In Jia was Chen Xinxue, appointed magistrate but went home without taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 其友周卜歷舉鄉試，知內黃，以父喪歸裏。

translations.literal: His friend Zhou Bolü passed the provincial examination, became magistrate of Neihuang, and returned home for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Zhou Bolü passed the provincial examination, became Neihuang magistrate, and went home for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 自成陷郟，執兩人欲官之，心學不從被殺。

translations.literal: When Zicheng took Jia he seized the two men and wished to give them office; Xinxue would not obey and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng took Jia he seized both and offered office; Xinxue refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 自成謂卜歷曰：「為我執知縣來，可代汝死。」

translations.literal: Zicheng said to Bolü: "Bring the magistrate to me and you may die in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng told Bolü, "Fetch the magistrate for me and you may die in his stead.

sentences.zh: 曰：「戕人以利己，仁者不為。」

translations.literal: He said: "To harm another for one's own benefit—no benevolent man would do it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "To harm another for one's own gain—no benevolent man would do it."

sentences.zh: 賊怒，並殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in anger killed them both.

sentences.zh: 汝所轄四邑並陷。

translations.literal: The four counties under his jurisdiction all fell.
translations.idiomatic: All four counties under his jurisdiction fell.

sentences.zh: 寶豐知縣張人龍，遵化人。

translations.literal: Baofeng Magistrate Zhang Renlong was a native of Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Baofeng Magistrate Zhang Renlong was from Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 城陷，不屈死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 妻年少，悍奴四人欲亂之。

translations.literal: His wife was young; four fierce slaves wished to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was young; four brutal slaves meant to violate her.

sentences.zh: 妻飲以酒俾極歡，潛遣婢告丞尉，捕殺奴，乃扶櫬旋裏。

translations.literal: The wife gave them wine until they were thoroughly merry, secretly sent a maid to inform the assistant and constable, had the slaves seized and killed, then escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: She plied them with wine until they were drunk, secretly sent a maid to the officials, had the slaves killed, then bore the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 魯山知縣楊呈芳，山海衛人，有惠政。

translations.literal: Lushan Magistrate Yang Chengfang was a native of Shanhai Guard and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan Magistrate Yang Chengfang was from Shanhai Guard and ruled humanely.

sentences.zh: 練總詹思鸞與進士宗麟祥等謀不軌，呈芳捕斬之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhan Siluan and metropolitan graduate Zong Linxiang and others plotted rebellion; Chengfang seized and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhan Siluan and graduate Zong Linxiang plotted rebellion; Chengfang seized and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 城陷，死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he died.

sentences.zh: 伊陽知縣孔貞璞，曲阜人。

translations.literal: Yiyang Magistrate Kong Zhenpu was a native of Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang Magistrate Kong Zhenpu was from Qufu.

sentences.zh: 賊薄城，以守禦堅，解圍去。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed the city the defense was firm and they lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels pressed the walls the defense held and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 他日有事汝陽，道遇賊，被執，亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Another day when there was trouble at Ruyang he met bandits on the road, was seized, and again refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on business at Ruyang, he met rebels on the road, was seized, and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 寶豐之陷也，舉人李得笥短衣雜眾中，為所執。

translations.literal: When Baofeng fell the graduate Li Desi, in short clothes among the crowd, was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Baofeng fell graduate Li Desi, dressed plainly among the crowd, was seized.

sentences.zh: 賊謀主牛金星者，故舉人也，勸賊重用舉人，賊所至獲舉人，即授以官。

translations.literal: Niu Jinxing, the bandits' chief strategist, was formerly a provincial graduate; he urged the bandits to make heavy use of graduates; wherever the bandits went, if they captured a graduate they gave him office.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinxing, the rebel strategist, had been a provincial graduate; he urged heavy use of graduates; wherever they went, graduates were given office.

sentences.zh: 得笥終不自言，賊莫知其為舉人也，役使之，不肯，伺賊寐將刺之，賊覺，被殺。

translations.literal: Desi never revealed himself; the bandits did not know he was a graduate and made him serve; he would not; he waited until the bandits slept to stab them; they awoke and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Desi never revealed himself; the rebels did not know he was a graduate and set him to labor; he refused; he waited until they slept to stab them; they awoke and killed him.

sentences.zh: 或告賊曰：「此舉人也。」

translations.literal: Someone told the bandits: "This man is a graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the rebels, "This man is a graduate.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，棄其屍而去。

translations.literal: The bandits were afraid and abandoned his corpse and left.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were afraid and abandoned his body.

sentences.zh: 時中州舉人盡節者，南陽張鳳翷、王明物，洛陽張民表，永城夏雲醇，商城余容善，光州王者琯，光山胡植，嵩縣王翼明，並罵賊死。

translations.literal: At that time among central-plain graduates who died for integrity were Zhang Fenghang and Wang Mingwu of Nanyang, Zhang Minbiao of Luoyang, Xia Yunchun of Yongcheng, Yu Rongshan of Shangcheng, Wang Zheguan of Guangzhou, Hu Zhi of Guangshan, and Wang Yiming of Song County—all cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Central-plain graduates who died for integrity included Zhang Fenghang and Wang Mingwu of Nanyang, Zhang Minbiao of Luoyang, Xia Yunchun of Yongcheng, Yu Rongshan of Shangcheng, Wang Zheguan of Guangzhou, Hu Zhi of Guangshan, and Wang Yiming of Song—all reviled the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 魯世任，字愧尹，垣曲人。

translations.literal: Lu Shiren, courtesy name Kuiyin, was a native of Yuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shiren, style name Kuiyin, was from Yuanqu.

sentences.zh: 性端方，事親孝。

translations.literal: His nature was upright; he was filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Upright by nature, he was filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 從安邑曹於汴學，又交絳州辛全，學日有聞。

translations.literal: He studied under Cao Yubian of Anyi and also associated with Xin Quan of Jiangzhou; his learning daily advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Cao Yubian of Anyi and befriended Xin Quan of Jiangzhou; his learning grew daily.

sentences.zh: 天啟末舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年知鄭州，建天中書院，集士子講肄其中，遠近從學者千人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he became magistrate of Zhengzhou, built the Tianzhong Academy, gathered students to lecture and study there, and a thousand came from near and far.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year ten he became Zhengzhou magistrate, built the Tianzhong Academy, and a thousand students came from near and far.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，給事中範士髦薦世任及臨城諸生喬己百、內丘太原通判喬中和於朝，稱為德行醇儒，堪繼薛瑄、陳獻章之後。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year Supervising Secretary Fan Shimao recommended Shiren, the Lincheng student Qiao Jibai, and the Neiqiu Taiyuan Vice Prefect Qiao Zhonghe to the court, calling them pure Confucians in virtue and conduct fit to follow Xue Xuan and Chen Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year thirteen Fan Shimao recommended Shiren, student Qiao Jibai, and vice prefect Qiao Zhonghe as pure Confucians fit to follow Xue Xuan and Chen Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 乞召試平臺，置左右備顧問，不報。

translations.literal: He asked that they be summoned to the Pingtai for examination and placed at the Emperor's side as advisers; no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: He asked they be tested at court and kept as advisers; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 十五年，流賊來犯，世任勒民兵禦之河干，戰敗自剄死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year roving bandits came to attack; Shiren led local militia to resist them at the river bank, was defeated in battle, and cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen roving rebels attacked; Shiren led militia at the river, was defeated, and cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 士民祀之書院中。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners worshipped him in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: The people enshrined him in the academy.

sentences.zh: 其年正月，賊陷襄城，知縣曹思正被殺，訓導張信罵賊不屈死，典史趙鳳豸拒賊死。

translations.literal: That year in the first month the bandits took Xiangcheng; Magistrate Cao Sizheng was killed; Instructor Zhang Xin cursed the bandits and died refusing to yield; Registrar Zhao Fengzhi resisted the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: That first month the rebels took Xiangcheng; Magistrate Cao Sizheng was killed; Instructor Zhang Xin reviled them and died; Registrar Zhao Fengzhi resisted and died.

sentences.zh: 復陷西華，知縣劉伯驂懷印投井死。

translations.literal: They again took Xihua; Magistrate Liu Boxiang embraced the seal and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: They again took Xihua; Magistrate Liu Boxiang clasped the seal and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 明年，汜水陷，知縣周騰蛟亦死焉。

translations.literal: The following year when Sishui fell Magistrate Zhou Tengjiao also died there.
translations.idiomatic: The next year when Sishui fell Magistrate Zhou Tengjiao died as well.

sentences.zh: 伯驂，河間人。

translations.literal: Boxiang was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 由歲貢生得官。

translations.literal: He received office through the annual tribute-student selection.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through the annual tribute selection.

sentences.zh: 賊信急，遣妻奉母歸。

translations.literal: When bandit intelligence was urgent he sent his wife to escort his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel alarms grew urgent he sent his wife to escort his mother home.

sentences.zh: 及城被困，有勸出降者，立斬之，登陴死守。

translations.literal: When the city was besieged some urged surrender; he immediately beheaded them and mounted the battlements to die in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was besieged some urged surrender; he beheaded them at once and mounted the walls to die defending.

sentences.zh: 賊驅其下為十覆，叠攻之，城遂陷，抗節死。

translations.literal: The bandits drove their subordinates in ten successive waves of attack; the city then fell; he died holding to his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove ten successive assaults; the city fell; he died holding his integrity.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟，香河舉人。

translations.literal: Tengjiao was a provincial graduate of Xianghe.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao was a Xianghe provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 邑兵荒，撫字有術，以其間厘定徭役，民甚便之。

translations.literal: The district suffered soldiers and famine; he governed with skill and in the interval fixed corvée labor; the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The district knew war and famine; he governed skillfully and fixed corvée labor; the people were greatly eased.

sentences.zh: 城孤懸河畔，縣人吳邦清等於城南立七砦相掎角，摩天砦最險。

translations.literal: The city stood isolated on the riverbank; Wu Bangqing and others of the county established seven stockades south of the city in mutual support; Motian Stockade was the most perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood alone on the river; Wu Bangqing and others built seven stockades south of town in mutual support; Motian Stockade was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 土寇李際遇伺騰蛟往河北，急據之，遂攻縣城。

translations.literal: The local bandit Li Jiyu, watching for Tengjiao's departure to Hebei, quickly seized it and then attacked the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandit Li Jiyu, seeing Tengjiao go to Hebei, seized Motian Stockade and attacked the county seat.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟聞，力請於上官，救兵至，始解去。

translations.literal: When Tengjiao heard he urgently pleaded with his superiors; relief troops arrived and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao urgently pleaded with superiors; relief came and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟念故城難守，遷縣治於摩天砦以扼賊沖。

translations.literal: Tengjiao, thinking the old city hard to defend, moved the county seat to Motian Stockade to block the bandit corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking the old city indefensible, Tengjiao moved the seat to Motian Stockade to block the rebel corridor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊大至，持十余日，勢且不支，砦臨河，可渡以免。

translations.literal: Before long bandits came in force; they held more than ten days; the situation could not be sustained; the stockade faced the river and one could cross to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels came in force; they held ten days but could not endure; the stockade faced the river and escape was possible.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟曰：「吾何忍舍眾獨生！」

translations.literal: Tengjiao said: "How can I bear to abandon the crowd and live alone!
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao said, "How can I abandon the people and live alone!

sentences.zh: 遂自投於河。

translations.literal: He then threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 賊退，人從河濱獲其屍，印懸肘間。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew people recovered his corpse from the riverbank; the seal hung at his elbow.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew his body was recovered from the river; the seal hung at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 河南凡八郡，三在河北，自六年蹂躪後，賊未再犯。

translations.literal: In all Henan had eight prefectures; three were north of the river; after the ravaging of the sixth year the bandits did not attack again.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had eight prefectures; three lay north of the river; after the ravaging of year six rebels did not return there.

sentences.zh: 其南五郡十一州七十三縣，靡不殘破，有再破三破者。

translations.literal: Of the five southern prefectures, eleven departments, and seventy-three counties, none escaped ruin; some were taken twice or thrice.
translations.idiomatic: The five southern prefectures, eleven departments, and seventy-three counties were all ruined; some fell two or three times.

sentences.zh: 城郭丘墟，人民百不存一。

translations.literal: Walls and moats became ruins; not one in a hundred of the people remained.
translations.idiomatic: Walls became ruins; scarcely one person in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦不復設官。

translations.literal: The court also ceased to appoint officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court ceased appointing officials.

sentences.zh: 間有設者，不敢至其地，遙寄治他所。

translations.literal: When officials were occasionally appointed they dared not go to the place and governed remotely from elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When officials were named they dared not go and governed from afar.

sentences.zh: 其遺黎僅存者，率結山寨自保，多者數千人，少者數百。

translations.literal: The remnant people who survived mostly formed mountain stockades for self-defense; the larger had several thousand men, the smaller several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors mostly formed mountain stockades; the largest had thousands, the smallest hundreds.

sentences.zh: 最大者，洛陽則際遇，汝寧則沈萬登，南陽則劉洪起兄弟，各擁眾數萬，而諸小寨悉歸之。

translations.literal: The largest were Jiyu at Luoyang, Shen Wandeng at Runan, and the Liu Hongqi brothers at Nanyang, each with tens of thousands, and the smaller stockades all submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest were Jiyu at Luoyang, Shen Wandeng at Runan, and the Liu Hongqi brothers at Nanyang, each with tens of thousands; smaller stockades submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 或附賊，或受朝命，陰陽觀望。

translations.literal: Some attached to bandits, some received court commissions, watching which way the wind blew.
translations.idiomatic: Some joined rebels, some took court commissions, watching which way fortune turned.

sentences.zh: 獨洪起嘗官副總兵，頗恭順。

translations.literal: Only Hongqi had once been Vice Regional Commander and was rather deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hongqi had been vice regional commander and was comparatively deferential.

sentences.zh: 其後諸人自相吞並，中原禍亂於是為極。

translations.literal: Later these men devoured one another in turn, and calamity in the central plain reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Later they devoured one another, and central-plain calamity reached its height.

sentences.zh: 至十六年四月，帝特下詔蠲五郡賦三年，諭諸人赦其罪，斬偽官者受職，捕賊徒者賫金，復城獻俘者不次擢用，然事已不可為矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year the Emperor specially issued an edict remitting three years of taxes in the five prefectures, pardoning the people's crimes, granting office to those who beheaded false officials, rewarding gold for capturing bandit followers, and promoting without regard to rank those who restored cities and presented captives—but the matter was already beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year sixteen the Emperor remitted three years' taxes in the five prefectures, pardoned crimes, granted office for beheading puppet officials, rewarded gold for capturing rebels, and promised extraordinary promotion for restoring cities—but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 劉禋，字誠吾，中部人。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, courtesy name Chengwu, was a native of Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, style name Chengwu, was from Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 祖仕，刑部郎中，以諍大禮廷杖。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi served as Director in the Ministry of Justice and was beaten at court for remonstrating on the Great Rites controversy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi was a Ministry of Justice director beaten at court in the Great Rites controversy.

sentences.zh: 後與定李福達獄，下吏遣戍。

translations.literal: Later, in deciding the Li Fuda case, he was sent down to the judiciary and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Li Fuda case, he was imprisoned and exiled.

sentences.zh: 穆宗朝起太仆少卿，不就。

translations.literal: In the Muzong reign he was summoned as Junior Director of the Stud but would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Under Muzong he was summoned as Junior Director of the Stud but refused.

sentences.zh: 父爾完，歷知商丘、名山，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Erwan successively served as magistrate of Shangqiu and Mingshan and had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Erwan had been magistrate of Shangqiu and Mingshan and was a man of learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 禋性孝，母歿於名山，四千里扶櫬，過劍閣雲棧，以肩任之。

translations.literal: Yin was filial by nature; when his mother died at Mingshan he carried the coffin four thousand li, passing Sword Gate and the cloud ladders, bearing it on his shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Filial by nature, when his mother died at Mingshan he carried the coffin four thousand li over Sword Gate and the cloud ladders on his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 父少寐，愛聽《史記》，禋每夕朗誦，俟父熟寢乃已，崇禎四年，賊陷中部，禋負父走免。

translations.literal: His father slept lightly and loved to hear the Records of the Grand Historian; each evening Yin read aloud and only stopped when his father was fast asleep; in the fourth year of Chongzhen bandits took Zhongbu and Yin carried his father on his back and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His father slept lightly and loved the Records of the Grand Historian; Yin read aloud each night until his father slept; in Chongzhen year four rebels took Zhongbu and Yin carried his father to safety.

sentences.zh: 十四年由鄉舉授登封知縣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year through the provincial examination he was appointed magistrate of Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he became Dengfeng magistrate through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 土寇為亂，禋練壯士，且守且戰，寇不敢近。

translations.literal: Local bandits rose in disorder; Yin drilled stalwart men and both defended and fought; the bandits did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits rebelled; Yin drilled stalwarts and fought and defended; bandits dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 十五年，李自成陷其城，禋被縛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Li Zicheng took his city; Yin was bound.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Li Zicheng took his city; Yin was bound.

sentences.zh: 自成以同郡故欲降之，禋叱曰：「豈有奕世清白吏肯降賊耶！」

translations.literal: Zicheng, as a fellow townsman, wished to induce his surrender; Yin rebuked him: "How could an official of spotless integrity for generations yield to bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng, as a fellow townsman, wished to win him over; Yin cried, "How could a spotless official of generations yield to rebels!

sentences.zh: 自成義之，遣賊將反覆說，禋執彌厲，乃見殺。

translations.literal: Zicheng honored him and sent a bandit general to persuade him again and again; Yin held all the firmer and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng honored him and sent generals again and again; Yin held firmer still and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陳顯元者，由副榜授新安知縣。

translations.literal: Chen Xianyuan had entered office through the supplementary list and was appointed magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianyuan entered through the supplementary list and became Xin'an magistrate.

sentences.zh: 惡衣糲食，徒步咨疾苦。

translations.literal: He wore coarse clothes and ate plain food and went on foot to inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He wore coarse clothes, ate plain food, and walked the district to hear people's woes.

sentences.zh: 以城堞傾頹，寇至不能守，率士民入保闕門寨。

translations.literal: Because the battlements were crumbling and bandits could not be held off when they came, he led gentry and people into Quemen Stockade for protection.
translations.idiomatic: With crumbling walls he could not hold the city; he led gentry and people into Quemen Stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊檄降，立碎其檄。

translations.literal: The bandits sent a summons to surrender; he immediately tore it to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent a surrender summons; he tore it to pieces.

sentences.zh: 及來犯，死守月余，力竭而陷。

translations.literal: When they came to attack he held firm for more than a month; his strength exhausted, the stockade fell.
translations.idiomatic: When they attacked he held more than a month; strength failed and the stockade fell.

sentences.zh: 見賊怒罵。

translations.literal: When he saw the bandits he cursed them in anger.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the rebels he reviled them.

sentences.zh: 賊大殺寨中人，顯元叱曰：「守寨者，我也。

translations.literal: The bandits massacred the people in the stockade; Xianyuan rebuked them: "Those who held the stockade—it was I.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massacred the stockade; Xianyuan cried, "I held this stockade.

sentences.zh: 百姓何辜，寧殺我！」

translations.literal: The common people are innocent—better kill me!
translations.idiomatic: The people are innocent—kill me instead!

sentences.zh: 賊怒，遂支解而死。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger then dismembered him and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in fury cut him apart.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河南被賊尤酷，故死事者尤多，其傳隸未詳者，開封之陷，則同知蘇茂均，通判彭士奇，大使徐升、閻生白皆死之。

translations.literal: At that time Henan suffered especially cruelly from bandits, and therefore those who died for the state were especially many; for those whose biographies are not given in detail, when Kaifeng fell Vice Magistrate Su Maojun, Vice Prefect Peng Shiji, and Grand Masters Xu Sheng and Yan Shengbai all died.
translations.idiomatic: Henan suffered especially from rebels, so deaths for the state were especially many; among those not detailed here, when Kaifeng fell Vice Magistrate Su Maojun, Vice Prefect Peng Shiji, and Grandees Xu Sheng and Yan Shengbai died.

sentences.zh: 士奇，高要人，由鄉舉。

translations.literal: Shiji was a native of Gaoyao and had entered office through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was from Gaoyao and entered through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 河南之陷，則先後知府亢孟檜、王蔭長，通判白守文，訓導張道脈，靈寶知縣朱挺，或被執不屈，或陷城自盡。

translations.literal: When Henan fell, the successive prefects Kang Menggui and Wang Yinzhang, Vice Prefect Bai Shouwen, Instructor Zhang Daomai, and Lingbao Magistrate Zhu Ting were either seized and refused to yield or, when the city fell, killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan fell, prefects Kang Menggui and Wang Yinzhang, Vice Prefect Bai Shouwen, Instructor Zhang Daomai, and Lingbao Magistrate Zhu Ting were seized and refused to yield or killed themselves when cities fell.

sentences.zh: 孟檜，臨汾人。

translations.literal: Menggui was a native of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: Menggui was from Linfen.

sentences.zh: 蔭長，吳橋人。

translations.literal: Yinzhang was a native of Wuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhang was from Wuqiao.

sentences.zh: 並由鄉舉。

translations.literal: Both had entered office through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Both entered through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 南陽之陷，則葉縣知縣張我翼被害，新野先後知縣陳公、丘茂表皆死之。

translations.literal: When Nanyang fell, Ye County Magistrate Zhang Woyi was killed; the successive magistrates of Xinye, Chen Gong and Qiu Maobiao, both died.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanyang fell Ye County Magistrate Zhang Woyi was killed; Xinye magistrates Chen Gong and Qiu Maobiao both died.

sentences.zh: 汝寧之陷，武臣則遊擊朱崇祖，千戶劉懋勛、楊紹祖、袁永基同子世蔭，百戶葉榮蔭、張承德、李衍壽、閻忠國，皆力戰死。

translations.literal: When Runan fell, among military officers the Mobile Corps Commander Zhu Chongzu, centurions Liu Maoxun, Yang Shaozu, and Yuan Yongji together with his son Shiyin, and company commanders Ye Rongyin, Zhang Chengde, Li Yanshou, and Yan Zhongguo all died fighting hard.
translations.idiomatic: When Runan fell, mobile corps commander Zhu Chongzu, centurions Liu Maoxun, Yang Shaozu, and Yuan Yongji with his son Shiyin, and company commanders Ye Rongyin, Zhang Chengde, Li Yanshou, and Yan Zhongguo all died fighting.

sentences.zh: 崇祖妻孫、永基母王亦死之。

translations.literal: Chongzu's wife Sun and Yongji's mother Wang also died.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu's wife Sun and Yongji's mother Wang died as well.

sentences.zh: 歲貢生林景昜，國學生趙得庚、楊道臨等，諸生趙重明、費明棟、楊應禎、李士諤等，皆死之。

translations.literal: The annual tribute student Lin Jingyi, Imperial Academy students Zhao Degeng and Yang Daolin, and students Zhao Chongming, Fei Mingdong, Yang Yingzhen, and Li Shie all died.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute student Lin Jingyi, academy students Zhao Degeng and Yang Daolin, and students Zhao Chongming, Fei Mingdong, Yang Yingzhen, and Li Shie all died.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史蘇京奉詔錄上，凡二百四十九人。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Su Jing received the imperial order to record and submit them; in all two hundred forty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Su Jing was ordered to record and submit the list: two hundred forty-nine in all.

sentences.zh: 後因國變，諸籍散佚。

translations.literal: Later, because of the dynastic collapse, the registers were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with the dynastic collapse, the registers were lost.

sentences.zh: 蓋武職及州縣末秩、舉貢諸生，所遺者幾什之五六。

translations.literal: Thus for military officers and the lowest ranks of prefectures and counties, graduates and students, roughly five or six tenths of those who died are preserved in the record.
translations.idiomatic: For military officers, low county ranks, graduates, and students, only about five or six tenths of the dead remain on record.

sentences.zh: 何燮，字中理，晉江人。

translations.literal: He Xie, courtesy name Zhongli, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Xie, style name Zhongli, was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，知亳州。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he was magistrate of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era he was magistrate of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州自八年後，寇賊交橫，益以饑饉，民死徙過半。

translations.literal: From the eighth year onward bandits and roving rebels crisscrossed the prefecture; famine was added, and more than half the people died or fled.
translations.idiomatic: From year eight onward rebels crisscrossed the prefecture; famine followed, and more than half the people died or fled.

sentences.zh: 燮盡心拊循，營戰守具甚備。

translations.literal: Xie devoted himself to comforting and governing them and made very complete preparations for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xie devoted himself to relief and made thorough preparations for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，山東、河南土寇叠至，燮戰盧家廟，生擒賊魁二人，刳其腸示眾，撫降者數千人。

translations.literal: Before long local bandits from Shandong and Henan came in waves; Xie fought at Lujia Temple, captured two bandit chiefs alive, disemboweled them to show the crowd, and pacified several thousand who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shandong and Henan bandits came in waves; at Lujia Temple Xie captured two chiefs alive, disemboweled them before the crowd, and pacified several thousand surrendering men.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，李自成陷河南，居民望風逃竄，城空不能守。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Li Zicheng took Henan; the inhabitants fled at the sight of the wind; the city was empty and could not be defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year fifteen Li Zicheng took Henan; people fled; the city emptied and could not be held.

sentences.zh: 賊至，執燮欲降之，罵不屈，斷足剖胸而死，懸首市上三日，耳鼻猶動。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived they seized Xie and wished to induce his surrender; he cursed and would not yield; they cut off his feet and opened his chest and he died; his head was hung in the market for three days and his ears and nose still moved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized him and urged surrender; he reviled them and would not yield; they cut off his feet and opened his chest; his head hung in the market three days, ears and nose still twitching.

sentences.zh: 賊遂縱兵四出，霍丘、靈璧、盱眙皆陷。

translations.literal: The bandits then spread their troops in all directions; Huoqiu, Lingbi, and Xuyi all fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then ravaged outward; Huoqiu, Lingbi, and Xuyi all fell.

sentences.zh: 霍丘，八年春嘗陷，至是再陷。

translations.literal: Huoqiu had once fallen in the spring of the eighth year; now it fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Huoqiu had fallen once in the spring of year eight; now it fell again.

sentences.zh: 知縣左相申率兵巷戰，力屈死之。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zuo Xiangshen led troops in lane fighting and died when his strength gave out.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zuo Xiangshen fought in the alleys and died when his strength failed.

sentences.zh: 巡檢吳姓者，鬥死。

translations.literal: An inspector surnamed Wu died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: An inspector surnamed Wu died in combat.

sentences.zh: 靈璧知縣唐良銳，全州舉人。

translations.literal: Lingbi Magistrate Tang Liangrui was a provincial graduate of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbi Magistrate Tang Liangrui was a Quanzhou provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 城陷，抗罵死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he resisted and cursed and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he resisted, reviled them, and died.

sentences.zh: 盱眙，先被陷，賊至，士民悉走，獨主簿胡淵不去。

translations.literal: Xuyi had been taken earlier; when the bandits came gentry and commoners all fled; only Registrar Hu Yuan did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi had fallen earlier; when rebels came everyone fled; only Registrar Hu Yuan remained.

sentences.zh: 縣故無城，淵持戟至龜山寺力鬥，殪數人。

translations.literal: The county had no wall; Yuan took a halberd to Guishan Temple and fought hard, killing several men.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no wall; Yuan took a halberd to Guishan Temple and killed several men.

sentences.zh: 賊駭欲遁，會馬蹶被執，奮罵而死。

translations.literal: The bandits in terror wished to flee; just then his horse stumbled and he was seized; he struggled and cursed and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked and meant to flee; his horse stumbled and he was seized; he fought and reviled them and died.

sentences.zh: 淵，永年人，起家貢生。

translations.literal: Yuan was a native of Yongnian and had begun his career as a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was from Yongnian and had entered office as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 趙興基，雲南太和人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingji was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingji was from Taihe in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，以鄉舉通判廬州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen through the provincial examination he became Vice Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he became Luzhou vice prefect through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 賀一龍、左金王等五部據英、霍二山，暑入秋出以為常。

translations.literal: He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and five other bands held the Ying and Huo mountains; it was their custom to enter in summer and leave in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and five bands held the Ying and Huo mountains, entering in summer and leaving in autumn.

sentences.zh: 督師楊嗣昌遣監軍僉事楊卓然招之，受侮而返。

translations.literal: Supervising Commander Yang Sichang sent Supervising Assistant Commissioner Yang Zhuoran to induce them to surrender; he was insulted and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang sent Yang Zhuoran to induce surrender; he was insulted and returned.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月襲陷英山，知縣高在飖抗賊死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year they raided and took Yingshan; Magistrate Gao Zaiyao resisted the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year fourteen they seized Yingshan; Magistrate Gao Zaiyao resisted and died.

sentences.zh: 十二月陷潛山，知縣李胤嘉、典史沈所安素苛急，奸民導賊執之，並不屈死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they took Qianshan; Magistrate Li Yinjia and Registrar Shen Suoan were harsh by nature; wicked men guided the bandits to seize them; both refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they took Qianshan; Magistrate Li Yinjia and Registrar Shen Suoan were harsh; traitors guided the rebels to seize them; both refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 所安子亦死焉。

translations.literal: Suoan's son also died.
translations.idiomatic: Suoan's son died as well.

sentences.zh: 十五年，張獻忠為左良玉所敗，走與諸部合，遂以三月攻舒城。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhang Xianzhong was defeated by Zuo Liangyu, fled, joined the other bands, and in the third month attacked Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Zhang Xianzhong was beaten by Zuo Liangyu, fled, joined other bands, and in the third month attacked Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 逾月城陷，改為得勝州，據之。

translations.literal: After more than a month the city fell; it was renamed Desheng Prefecture and they held it.
translations.idiomatic: After a month the city fell; they renamed it Desheng Prefecture and held it.

sentences.zh: 遣其黨分掠旁邑，遊騎日抵廬州城下。

translations.literal: He sent his partisans to plunder neighboring counties; roving horsemen daily reached the foot of Luzhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: He sent partisans to plunder neighboring counties; raiders daily reached Luzhou's walls.

sentences.zh: 興基與知府鄭履祥、經歷鄭元綬、合肥知縣潘登貴、指揮同知趙之璞、裏居參政程楷分門守。

translations.literal: Xingji together with Prefect Zheng Luxiang, Administrator Zheng Yuanshou, Hefei Magistrate Pan Denggui, Assistant Commander Zhao Zhipu, and retired Administrator Cheng Kai held divided defense at each gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji with Prefect Zheng Luxiang, Administrator Zheng Yuanshou, Hefei Magistrate Pan Denggui, Assistant Commander Zhao Zhipu, and retired Administrator Cheng Kai held each gate.

sentences.zh: 監司蔡如蘅貪戾，民不附，賊諜滿城中不能知。

translations.literal: Supervisor Cai Ruheng was greedy and cruel; the people did not attach themselves to him; bandit spies filled the city and he could not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Cai Ruheng was greedy and cruel; the people would not follow him; rebel spies filled the city unseen.

sentences.zh: 五月，提學御史徐之垣以試士至，獻忠遣其徒偽為諸生，襲儒冠以入，夜半舉炮，城中大擾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Educational Censor Xu Zhiyuan came to examine students; Xianzhong sent his followers disguised as students, wearing scholar caps to enter; at midnight they fired cannon and the city was thrown into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Educational Censor Xu Zhiyuan came to test students; Xianzhong sent men disguised as students in scholar caps; at midnight they fired cannon and the city erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 之垣、如蘅及履祥、登貴並縋城走。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan, Ruheng, Luxiang, and Denggui all lowered themselves from the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan, Ruheng, Luxiang, and Denggui all fled over the wall.

sentences.zh: 興基時守水西門，聞變，挺刃下戍樓與鬥，斬數人，被創死。

translations.literal: Xingji was then holding the west water gate; hearing the alarm he drew his blade, came down from the watchtower to fight, cut down several men, was wounded, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji held the west water gate; hearing the alarm he drew his blade, descended to fight, killed several men, took wounds, and died.

sentences.zh: 元綬、楷共守南薰門，元綬力鬥死，楷不屈死。

translations.literal: Yuanshou and Kai together held the Nanxun Gate; Yuanshou fought hard and died; Kai refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou and Kai held the Nanxun Gate together; Yuanshou fought hard and died; Kai refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 之璞守東門，巷戰死。

translations.literal: Zhipu held the east gate, fought in the lanes, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhipu held the east gate, fought in the alleys, and died.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勢連陷含山、巢縣、廬江及無為、六安，又陷太湖。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the momentum and in succession took Hanshan, Chaoxian, Lujiang, and Wuwei and Lu'an, and again took Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed on to take Hanshan, Chaoxian, Lujiang, Wuwei, Lu'an, and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 知縣楊春芳、典史陳知訓、教諭沈鴻起、訓導婁懋履並死焉。

translations.literal: Magistrate Yang Chunfang, Registrar Chen Zhixun, Instructor Shen Hongqi, and Instructor Lou Maoli all died there.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yang Chunfang, Registrar Chen Zhixun, Instructor Shen Hongqi, and Instructor Lou Maoli all died.

sentences.zh: 廬州城池高深。

translations.literal: The walls and moat of Luzhou were deep and high.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's walls were deep and high.

sentences.zh: 八年春，賊百方力攻，知府吳太樸堅守不下。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year the bandits attacked with every method and force; Prefect Wu Taipu held firm and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year eight rebels attacked with every method; Prefect Wu Taipu held firm and they could not take it.

sentences.zh: 後屢犯，終不得誌，至是以計得之。

translations.literal: Later they repeatedly attacked but never achieved their aim; now they obtained it by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked repeatedly without success; now they took it by trickery.

sentences.zh: 履祥、登貴懼罪，委之興基。

translations.literal: Luxiang and Denggui, fearing punishment, laid the blame on Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: Luxiang and Denggui, fearing blame, laid it on Xingji.

sentences.zh: 總督史可法察其冤以聞，乃治守令罪，而贈興基河南僉事，楷光祿卿，元綬亦贈恤。

translations.literal: Governor-General Shi Kefa investigated the injustice and reported it; the defending officials were then punished, while Xingji was posthumously granted Henan Assistant Commissioner, Kai Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Yuanshou also received posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shi Kefa investigated and reported the injustice; the officials were punished, while Xingji was posthumously made Henan assistant commissioner, Kai Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Yuanshou honored as well.

sentences.zh: 方賊攻舒城，縣令適以憂去，裏居編修胡守恒與遊擊孔廷訓督民兵共守。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked Shucheng the magistrate had just left office in mourning; retired Compiler Hu Shouheng together with Mobile Corps Commander Kong Tingxun supervised local militia in joint defense.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Shucheng the magistrate was away in mourning; retired compiler Hu Shouheng and mobile corps commander Kong Tingxun led militia in defense.

sentences.zh: 會遊擊縱所部淫掠，士民遂叛降賊。

translations.literal: Just then the mobile corps let its men rape and plunder wantonly; gentry and commoners thereupon rebelled and surrendered to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The mobile corps let its men rape and plunder; the people rebelled and surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，悍卒殺守恒。

translations.literal: When the city was about to fall fierce soldiers killed Shouheng.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall fierce soldiers killed Shouheng.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈少詹事，謚文節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: On report he was posthumously made Junior Mentor with the posthumous title Wenjie.
